articleTitle: Influence of the Background Plasma on the Performance for X-Band Gyrotron Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: Analysis of the performance for X-band continuous wave gyrotron traveling wave tubes (gyro- TWTs) with background plasma caused by residual gas ionization discharge is presented in this paper. The residual gas is released from the lossy dielectric ceramics during high average or continuous wave operation and ionized by colliding with the high-energy gyrating electrons. This results in a deterioration in the quality of the interacting electrons, which leads to a decrease in the output power and spectrum performance of the gyro-TWT. The collision of these ionized residual gas with gyrating electrons had been simulated based on a simplified model and the results such as electron beam characteristics, output power and spectrum are given and analyzed.

articleTitle: TH1509U European 170 GHZ 1 MW CW Industrial Gyrotron Upgrade
abstract: This paper describes the status on the upgrade of the first European gyrotron prototype for ITER, manufactured by Thales. The upgraded prototype, TH1509U, is now being tested to verify the performance improvements and to assess the compliance with ITER ECRH requirements.

articleTitle: Low Cost Electron Gun for D-band Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: A D-band TWT (141 - 148.5 GHz) is the enabling device for a novel Point to multipoint sub-THz wireless network with multi Gigabit per second capacity in the frame of European Commission H2020 ULTRAWAVE project. TWTs for wireless applications due to the competitive market needs to be affordable and of easy fabrication. The electron gun is one of the most critical part of a TWT in terms of fabrication and cost. The design and fabrication of a new electron gun for D-band TWTs is presented. The simple structure of the electron gun is suitable for large production and low fabrication cost. The high voltage isolation is obtained by rings of ceramics. This avoid the need of potting as in conventional electron gun.

articleTitle: Development and Test of 175 GHz Clinotron Tube
abstract: The results of the development and test of a 175GHz CW clinotron with the output power level of 1W have been presented and discussed. The frequency tuning range from 168GHz to 179GHz and the spectral line width of about 1MHz was achieved with the help of PID feedback control realized in the high-voltage power supply. The experimental test showed the applicability of the designed 175GHz clinotron tube to the thermographic alignment of the quasi-optical transmission line of the CTS-diagnostic at the W7-X stellarator.

articleTitle: Feedback Effects on a Recirculating Planar Crossed-Field Amplifier (RPCFA)
abstract: The Recirculating Planar Crossed- Field Amplifier (RPCFA) is a high-power microwave amplifier. This paper presents the experimental configuration and results of an experiment to test the effects of signal feedback, as well as the design for a new double-sided RPCFA. With 100% feedback and zero drive power, the RPCFA is shown to oscillate. Adding attenuation in the feedback loop is shown to suppress the oscillation.

articleTitle: Progress in Development of Powerful Bragg FEL Operating from Sub-THz to THz Band
abstract: Project of sub-THz/THz band FEL driven by linac “LIU” 5 – 20 MeV / 2 kA / 200 ns is under development in collaboration of BINP RAS (Novosibirsk) and IAP RAS (N.Novgorod) and aimed to achieve sub-GW power and a record pulse energy content of ~10–100 J in these frequency band. Design of the FEL key components and operating parameters are presented, state of the project is discussed.

articleTitle: Numerical study on the formation of second virtual cathode by using different material floating zone plate inside drift tube region
abstract: In this study, a particle-in-cell simulation was carried out on an axial vircator by using MAGIC. A second virtual cathode (VC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) was formulated by using the escaping electrons from traditional VC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> as a wall charge accumulated at the floating zone plate designed at 3.42 GHz. The material of the opaque zones was changed to copper, aluminum, and glass to form a VC2 and power enhancement. The opaque zones with aluminum and copper behave as an obstacle at the new frequency by VC2 for the propagation of the electromagnetic wave. While the opaque zones with insulating material (glass) also contributed to forming VC2 and suitable for the power enhancement by VC2 at the new frequencies. These results are useful for a real expeiment.

articleTitle: A Self-Assembled High Current Si Field Emitter Array
abstract: A simple, low-cost fabrication technology to develop high packing density arrays of silicon nano-field-emitters based on top-down self-assembly is presented. Using Langmuir-Blodgett deposition technique, a packed monolayer of silica particles with an average diameter of 200 nm is deposited on a patterned Si substrate. Silica particles act as micro-masks during deep reactive ion etching of the silicon wafer. Length, diameter, and sharpness of the nano-field-emitters are optimized by adjusting etching conditions to achieve high current density, low turn-on voltage, and reliable performance. Field-emitter density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.6\times 10^{9}$</tex> tips/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a maximum measured current density of 13.1 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, corresponding to 8 nA/tip has been achieved. The average electric field for this measurement was as low as 3.5 V/μm.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of D-band Planar Double Microstrip Meander Line Slow Wave Structure
abstract: A double microstrip meander line (DMML) slow wave structure (SWS) for terahertz (THz) band traveling wave tube (TWT) is proposed in this paper. The DMML combines two symmetrically distributed microstrip meander line (MML) to provide a broaden transverse width for better interaction with sheet electron beam. The results of design and fabrication are reported. Electromagnetic characteristics show high slow wave factor and wide band operating for DMML SWS. Finished samples are fabricated by microfabrication processes based on magnetron sputtering, UV-lithography and ion beam etching.

articleTitle: Gap waveguides for millimeter wave slow wave structures
abstract: The use of groove gap waveguide technology is proposed to aid the design of wide band slow wave structures for millimeter wave travelling wave tubes. The possibility to control the electromagnetic wave without the need for metal contact at the walls can facilitate the realization at high frequencies while increasing design flexibility.

articleTitle: From 2D to 1.5D: Reduced Order Simulations with the Large-Signal Code TESLA
abstract: This work presents results of the study, which involves modifications in the algorithms of the well-known 2D large-signal klystron code TESLA with a goal to improve its performance by simplifications in the physics of its model. The proposed modifications are based on the idea to reduce number of degrees of freedom of particle's motion from 3 down to 1 by restricting their motion along Z-axis only. Essentially, this will assume that magnetic field is infinitely large and one can completely ignore radial motion of particles as they will be “frozen” and allowed move in one direction only. Such modification in effect will reduce dimensionality of the algorithm from 2D down to 1.5D as a price to pay for proposed simplifications in the model. We will discuss pilot results of modeling by using the modified, reduced order algorithm, making main emphasis on advantages and disadvantages (“gains and losses”) of such step.

articleTitle: A 1.3 GHz 100 kW Ultra-high Efficiency Klystron
abstract: Calabazas Creek Research, Inc. is developing a high efficiency, 1.3 GHz, 100 kW klystron for driving accelerators. A simulated efficiency of 79% was realized, and the device is being fabricated. Details of the design and available test results will be presented.

articleTitle: Development of Output Couplers for High-Power Ku/K Dual-Band TWT
abstract: A step-waveguide of smaller waveguide, used in the pillbox window for a wide bandwidth and large power capacity is presented in this paper. The output couplers, including the windows, impedance transformers, and a transition to Slow Wave Structure (SWS) have been designed, fabricated, and tested for a Ku/K Dual-Band TWT. The cold test of output section shows that the VSWR is less than 1.52:1in the whole operation frequency range.

articleTitle: A New IGBT Over-Voltage and Over-Current Protection Method Based on Active Clamp Technology
abstract: This paper describes a new insulated gate bipolar translators (IGBT) over-voltage and over-current protection method based on active clamp technology. This method can help to reduce the protection time of IGBT at over-voltage, which allows the protection circuit to protect the IGBT in hundreds of nanoseconds. The pulse modulator can be effectively protected when multiple IGBTs are used in series to form the pulse and prevent the damage of each device. Through the tests, superior characteristics of the proposed method has been confirmed.

articleTitle: Development of Ku-Band 200W radiation-cooled Space TWT
abstract: Traveling wave tube which use to amplify the microwave signal, In order to meet high-capacity requirement of communications satellite, a Ku-band 200W wave Space TWT has been designed in this paper. A dual-anode electronic gun, double taper helix slow wave structure, 4-stage depressed collector was successfully designed and developed to 200W, exceeded 67% overall efficiency at 1 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Failure Mechanism of Large Scale Field Emission Array
abstract: A 1000×1000 Si FEA went through reliability test. Under fixed gate-voltage, the emission current stays stable at ~3mA over 3 days, but suddenly dropped 92% within one second, while the gate leakage current drops simultaneously. Post-testing physical characterization reveals majority of the emitters within the array keeps their structure integrity. The sudden emission current drop is due to a small amount of shorted/damaged emitters on the edge of the array.

articleTitle: Design of a Sub-THz Extended Interaction Amplifier with Trapezoidal Structure
abstract: Due to the superior electromagnetic coupling characteristics, the subwavelength hole array structure has attracted widespread attention. In this paper, a new type of extended interaction amplifier (EIA) is designed by combining the subwavelength hole array structure with the trapezoidal line circuit. The resonant cavity simulation in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TM}_{31}-2\pi$</tex> mode of terahertz is analyzed. Through the 3D Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulation, when the input signal is 20-mW, the designed EIA can stably generate 10.25 W power, at 231.4 GHz, with 27.1-dB gain and almost 850 MHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Improved Numerical Algorithms for Child-Langmuir Emission
abstract: We present improved numerical algorithms for thermionic emission in the finite-element gun code MICHELLE. The improved algorithms employ newly implemented Child-Langmuir special functions and robust iterative solvers that quickly yield near double precision machine accuracy in analytic problems. The implementation in MICHELLE yields substantially improved current densities, reducing the 1% error observed in some cases to less than 0.25% error.

articleTitle: Test of G-band Folded Waveguide Traveling-wave Tube
abstract: Developing a traveling wave tube in the terahertz band is a challenging task. In this article, a G-band folded waveguide traveling wave tube is tested. Using a vector network analyzer to test the components of the TWT, the results of testing beryllium oxide window show that S11 is lower than −18dB and S21 is greater than −2dB, and the results of testing slow wave circuit show that S11 is lower than −15.6dB and S21 is greater than −11.8dB. The thermal test results show that the TWT oscillates. The maximum forward oscillation power is 110mW and the maximum reverse oscillation power is 36mW. The maximum single-frequency output power is 1.3mW at 208GHz when the TWT operates at 20.01kV.

articleTitle: Development of E-Band Continuous Wave Folded Waveguide TWT
abstract: An E-band 70W continuous wave folded waveguide TWT (CW FWTWT) was designed and fabricated. The measured results showed that beam transmission was over 98% at dc and better than 97% at the highest peak RF power. Measured output powers are higher than 76.7W with saturated gains higher than 31.1dB within frequency range of 81-86GHz. This TWT adopts single depressed collector and the total efficiencies are higher than 26.7% within 81-86GHz.

articleTitle: Monolithic Fabrication Concepts for a Ka-band Sheet-Beam Coupled-Cavity TWT
abstract: We report on efforts toward a monolithic Ka-band sheet-beam coupled-cavity TWT circuit. This new circuit serves as a drop-in replacement for a demonstrated device that was originally fabricated using the method of brazing stacked plates.

articleTitle: A Design of High-power and Wide-band Metamaterial Output Window at Ka-band
abstract: A design method of the metamaterial-based output window is analyzed. By the equivalent medium theory (EMT), the equivalent dielectric constant of the medium can be changed by its proportion. Compared with the traditional multi-layer window, the flexibility of this design is significantly improved. The simulated result has achieved a frequency bandwidth of about 7.5 GHz for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{11}$</tex> mode of the circular waveguide in the Ka-band. The measurement of the circular output window shows a −20 dB bandwidth of about 7 GHz. In addition, the thermal power capacity of this window is analyzed.

articleTitle: Grid-controlled Electron Gun for the S-band Reversed Cherenkov Oscillator
abstract: In this paper, a grid-controlled electron gun is designed and optimized to generate a pencil electron beam for the S-band reversed Cherenkov oscillator (RCO). Under the condition of the anode voltage of 29 kV, the simulation results show that the beam current is 6.8 A, the radius of the electron beam waist is about 1.7 mm, and the range is 18.71 mm. The facts demonstrate that the grid-controlled electron gun can meet the demands of the RCO with the average output power of 45 kW at 2.21 GHz. The RCO can be applied to particle accelerators, medical imaging, microwave heating, and so on.

articleTitle: Offset Double Corrugated Waveguide
abstract: The novel offset double corrugated waveguide is proposed as slow wave structure for wide band TWTs at sub-THz frequencies as enabling power amplifier for long range sub-THz links. The double corrugated waveguide has been conceived to relax the fabrication, main technological challenge for sub-THz vacuum tube realization, maintaining high performance. The offset double corrugated waveguide has the same advantages of the double corrugated waveguide in terms of fabrication, but it provides a higher interaction impedance. In the paper, the offset double corrugated waveguide has been designed and compared to the double corrugated waveguide in the 150 - 161 GHz frequency range, demonstrating the higher interaction impedance, beneficial for improving TWT performances.

articleTitle: Design Study of a 0.2-THz Traveling-Wave Tube With Multiple Sheet Electron Beam
abstract: In this article, we present the results of numerical design and modeling of an electron gun with an impregnated thermionic cathode producing a triple elliptic-shaped electron beam of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1\ \text{mm}\times 0.6\ \text{mm}$</tex> dimensions of each beamlet. Such a beam interacts with a higher-order TE30 mode of the dual-grating staggered slow-wave structure (SWS). The 0.2-THz SWS with dielectric absorbers to prevent backward-wave excitation of lower-order transverse modes is designed and simulated.

articleTitle: A Wiener-Arrhenius-Model-Based Method for Life Prediction of TWT Cathode
abstract: In this paper, in order to estimate the life of TWT quickly, an accelerated degradation test (ADT) was carried out applying a short vacuum tube, and a life prediction method based on the Wiener-Arrhenius model is proposed considering individual variability among the tested samples. The validity of the proposed method is verified through comparison with the extrapolation result of curve fitting under normal operating condition, and it is concluded that the Wiener-Arrhenius-model-based method is more accurate and reliable.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of Flattening Electrodes Temperature for Multistage Depressed Collectors
abstract: Hotspot, which can result in outgassing during multistage depressed collectors work, is undesirable for space travelling wave tube which of merits is high reliable. In the paper, flattening electrodes temperature was investigated during designing four-stage depressed collectors with high efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of the radio frequency section of a V-Band Klystron
abstract: This article presents the design and simulation results for the RF section of a V -band klystron operating at 60 GHz. Square shape single side reentrant cavities, compatible with micromachining fabrication process are proposed for radio frequency (RF) section of this device. The cavity parameters were obtained through optimization of cavity geometrical parameters, i.e. the interaction gap, cavity length, height etc. Design approach of the cavities as well as corresponding simulation results are presented. Initial result of the beam wave interaction, showing stable growth of the RF wave is also presented. The license-free frequencies at V -band are being increasingly relevant with the advent of 5G mm-wave communication technologies. This device may find application in establishment of high data rate mm-wave communication for back-haul/front-haul.

articleTitle: Adjoint Approach to Optimization and Sensitivity Analysis of External Circuit Effects in Vacuum Electronic Devices
abstract: We expand the adjoint approach to optimization and sensitivity analysis of beam-wave interaction in any vacuum electronic device (VED) that consists of a circuit interacting with a linear beam through a series of gaps. The method is based on the conservation of symplectic area for two perturbed solution of the Hamiltonian form of the equations that govern the beam-wave interaction. When the adjoint solution is obtained using a simulation code, it may be used to evaluate the multi-dimensional derivatives needed for efficient optimization and for sensitivity analysis. We focused on numerical implementation and study of the effects of external circuit variations what expressed as variation of gap-to-gap distances, gap size and impedance matrix of the external structure.

articleTitle: Multiple Beam Power Grid Tubes for High Frequency and High Power Operation
abstract: High power, high efficiency RF sources are required at frequencies below 700 MHz for ion and proton accelerators. These sources are also used for high energy accelerators, such as the Advanced Photon Source, which is seeking 350 MHz RF sources producing more than 200 kW of continuous power. The program is developing multiple beam triodes capable of providing this RF power at efficiencies exceeding 80%. The sources would be extremely compact and low cost. Both the triodes and the associated RF cavities are being developed.

articleTitle: Performance Expectation and Preparation of the First Experimental Campaign of the KIT 2 MW 170/204 GHz Coaxial-Cavity Gyrotron
abstract: The existing KIT 2 MW 170 GHz coaxial-cavity short-pulse pre-prototype gyrotron is being prepared to be upgraded towards multi-frequency operation at 170/204 GHz in the new FULGOR test facility. Therefore, each existing component was examined for the need for modification. A new anode, an elongation of the coaxial insert, the XY -table, and the HV oil tank have to be modified for the first operation. All required components are already manufactured and are prepared for assembly. In the first short-pulse experiments an RF output powers of 2.2 and 1.7 MW can be expected at 170 and 204 GHz, respectively. In a second experimental campaign the coaxial-cavity and the quasi-optical output system will be replaced for an optimized configuration achieving more than 2 MW RF output power at both frequencies.

articleTitle: Low-voltage Gyrotron as Simple Mm-Wave Source
abstract: Gyrotrons are commonly considered as expensive, bulky, and technically complicated devices due to high power, voltage, and high magnetic fields. However, if high output power is not needed, gyrotrons can look much simpler, and can operate at low voltage, despite the relativistic nature of induced cyclotron radiation explored. In this talk, the numerous theoretical and experimental results for low-voltage gyrotron operation are considered. Using accumulated experience, the feasibility of the millimeter-wave gyrotron with low voltage and power consumption is discussed.

articleTitle: Experimental tests of a high-stable 170 GHz/25 kW gyrotron as a master oscillator for frequency locking of megawatt level microwave sources
abstract: The paper presents the tests of a medium-powered 170 GHz gyrotron, which was developed as a master oscillator for frequency locking of megawatt-level sources. In the experiment, the output power of more than 25 kW with about 30% efficiency was obtained in CW mode. With the use of a PLL system, we stabilized this gyrotron frequency and demonstrated the spectrum width of less than 2 Hz, which corresponds to the relative value of about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−11</sup>.

articleTitle: Mechanical Design of the Short Pulse E×B Drift Two-Stage Depressed Collector Prototype for High Power Gyrotron
abstract: Multistage depressed collector (MDC) technology is capable of significantly increased overall tube efficiencies of vacuum electronic devices compared to conventional single stage depressed collectors (SDC). The spent electron beam sorting as used for TWT and klystron collectors is not effective in the high stray magnetic field of gyrotrons. For that reason, many new design approaches based on E×B drift concept have been theoretically investigated during the last years at KIT. The mechanical design for the first MDC for a high power gyrotron is finalized and the production started end of 2020. In this work, the fundamentals of the mechanical design and the cooling principle of the electrodes are presented.

articleTitle: The Effects of Angular Momentum on Multipactor in Coaxial Lines
abstract: This work will discuss the effects of angular momentum for the multipactor electrons in a coaxial line. In particular, analytical modeling of a multipactor discharge in the two-dimensional annular cross-sectional area of a coaxial transmission line will be considered. The strongly coupled governing equations of motion for the electrons may be decoupled and combined using techniques from the central-force problem in classical mechanics. A closed form approximate analytical formula for the multipactor electron trajectory will then be obtained from the resulting simplified orbital equation.

articleTitle: Validation of the Stability Analysis Framework Based on the Large-signal Code TESLA-Z by Its Application to the Experimental TWTs
abstract: We present results of an extensive validation study for the recently developed frequency-domain stability framework based on the NRL 2D large-signal code TESLA-Z used to determine stability of the given Vacuum Electronic Device (VED). The used in the stability framework approach is based on an idea of finding gain matrix G for the given circuit and then performing analysis of its eigenvalues g on the complex plane to find critical solutions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{g}\geq 1$</tex>, which indicates on instability of the device according to the Nyquist net encirclement criteria. To validate the newly developed stability framework we are applying it to the two experimental TWTs, designed and measured at NRL during the last decade. The predictions of performed stability analysis are compared with the measured performance of the devices and with predictions made by the in-house Particle-in-Cell (PIC) code Neptune.

articleTitle: Design of Microstrip Meander Line SWS with Fully Connected Auto-adaptive Neural Network
abstract: We report on the design and demonstration of a practical Fully Connected Auto-adaptive Deep Neural Network (FCADNN) for microstrip meander line (MML) slow-wave structures, which can be used to speed up the design process of MML-SWS with excellent performance. We train FCADNN to design MML-SWS using exact numerical simulation results in a form of supervised learning, which shows that the prediction error is lower than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1\%$</tex>. The simulation results show that the attenuation of the designed structure created by FCADNN is 1.44 dB/mm at 160GHz center frequency with the phase velocity and the pierce impedance is 0.2c and 16 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: Time-Domain non-linear simulations of a 3 meter long traveling wave tube
abstract: At previous IVEC conferences, we presented a new N-body time-domain model for simulating traveling wave tubes (TWTs), which has been applied and assessed for several industrial TWTs covering a broad range of bandwidth and power regimes. Since then, we applied this model to meters long TWTs operating far beyond the saturation point. The capacity of our algorithm DIMOHA to predict correctly non linear behaviours is assessed against measurements for a 200 MHz, 3 meter long TWT.

articleTitle: Dispersion Diagrams of Linear Slow-Wave Structures
abstract: Analytically calculated dispersion diagram of an over-moded nine-periods V-band slow-wave structure (SWS) designed to operate in a slow- or surface-wave TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf> mode is re-examined using two-dimensional Poisson SuperFish code allowing to precisely cal-culate electric field spatial patterns of all azimuthally-symmetric transverse-magnetic (TM) modes possible to exist in this SWS. It is shown that the analytically calculated dispersion curves of higher-order TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</inf> modes of the SWS are not the dispersion curves of pure TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</inf> modes, but fascinating combinations of themselves with dis-persion curves of all lower-order TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0(n-k)</inf> modes, where k= 1 … (n-1). Such, for example, an analytically calculated dispersion curve of TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf> mode is factually a combination of three different dispersion curves: (i) one of the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">031</inf> mode with 1=0 … 4, (ii) another one of the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</inf> mode with 1=5 … 7, and (iii) third one of the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">021</inf> mode with 1=8 … 9, where I is an axial index of axial TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n1</inf> modes.

articleTitle: Research progress of cathode for microwave tube at BVERI
abstract: This paper describes recent progress on the investigation of cathodes for microwave electronic device at BVERI. The key factors related to the cathode emission performance will be discussed. The current density of scandate cathode in diode and electron gun reaches 281A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 157A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> respectively, which has been widely used in high power multi-beam klystron, the lifetime is more than 3000h and the current density reaches 20–25 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> under the condition of pulse width 1ms, 10% duty ratio. The fast warm cathode for missile-borne traveling wave tube (TWT) can reach 1000 °C in 3 seconds. For the high reliable and low evaporation cathode in Airborne grid controlled TWT, the evaporation rate of Barium is 4.7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−11</sup> g/s.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The pulsed-current emission density of the oxide cathode prepared by plasma spraying process reaches 40.5A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Under the laser power of 5 W, the emission current of the field auxiliary photocathode fabricated by micromachining technology reaches 26mA.

articleTitle: Investigation on a 0.34THz Dual-Open-Cavity Extended Interaction Klystron
abstract: An extended interaction klystron (EIK) composed of two open-cavities is proposed and investigated in this paper. The open-cavity consists of an upper cylindrical mirror and two lines of grating, between which is a natural electron beam tunnel. The electron beam modulated by the input signal in the input cavity will produce a stable oscillating signal in the output cavity. The simulation results show that when the EIK works at 0.34 THz, the average output power can reach 2.4 W, the corresponding gain and electronic efficiency are 26.8 dB and 2.18%, respectively. This structure will be a possible direction for the development of terahertz radiation sources.

articleTitle: Outgassing of Electron Beam Printed Copper
abstract: Electron beam printing, or additive manufacturing, of oxygen-free high conductivity copper has demonstrated significant potential for utilization in vacuum electronic devices and their sub-components. Pioneering vacuum electronics community has influenced the additive manufacturing community to develop platforms and processes for printing copper and its alloys. Following demonstrations of ultra-high vacuum hermeticity and measurements of RF losses, evaluation of outgassing of additively manufactured X-band waveguides has been performed. Preliminary results reveal suitable outgassing rates for implementation in ultra-high vacuum systems.

articleTitle: Design Studies on 0.3- THz, 0.5-MW Conventional Cavity Gyrotron for Plasma Heating
abstract: The design aspects of the conventional interaction cavity and RF behavior studies of a 0.3- THz, 0.5-MW, TE41,12 mode gyrotron are presented. The study includes the mode selection, cold cavity calculation and single-mode calculations which are carried out using our in-house computer code package Gyrotron Design Suite (GDS-2018). Further, time-dependent multi-mode calculations (SELFT) are performed using the KIT SELFT code to verify power growth in the desired mode over the other competing modes.

articleTitle: Calculation Of The Characteristics Of The Electron Beam Formed By An Electron-Optical System With A Multi- Tip Field Emitter
abstract: Calculations of characteristics of an electron beam formed by an electron-optical system (EOS) with a multi-tip field emitter are presented. The calculations take into account the features of the emitter surface morphology.

articleTitle: Wideband Highly Efficient Ka-band 250 W Space Traveling-Wave Tube THL20250C & THL20250R
abstract: In satellite systems, on-board repeaters shall deliver always more RF power to increase satellite capacity for higher data transmission rate. To meet this demand, Thales A VS France has developed a wideband, highly efficient 250 W Ka-band Traveling Wave Tube (TWT), the new generation of space TWTs in Ka-band. Qualification of both conduction cooled (THL20250C) and radiation cooled (THL20250R) versions is running. The TWT delivers more than 250 W in narrow band (≤ 2 GHz) and more than 240 W in wide band (2.9 GHz). The main technical characteristics of the THL20250 family are described as well as the main performance over 2.9 GHz in Ka-band.

articleTitle: Measurements of the Breakdown Threshold for Coaxial Multipactor and the Delay for Multipactor Onset
abstract: Multipactor discharges can disrupt and damage satellite communications systems. This paper presents results for a 3.05-GHz coaxial multipactor test cell. The breakdown threshold has been measured and compared to previous CST Particle Studio simulations. Multipactor self-conditioning has been shown to increase the breakdown threshold and cause most of the experimental data to approach the simulation result to within approximately 10% at 4–6 kW power levels. Additional experiments for measuring and analyzing the delay for the onset of multipactor are discussed.

articleTitle: Study on Gate Modulation Property of Vacuum Field Emission Triode
abstract: An insulated-gate vacuum field emission triode with a nano-scale channel is proposed in this paper. The nano-scale channel of this vacuum triode is generated by using electro-forming process. Experimental results reveal that the fabricated device demonstrates a certain triode behavior of the gate modulation. Moreover, we further optimize the thickness of the insulator layer, demonstrating that the states of the proposed triode could be effectively modulated by bottom-gate bias. Fowler-Nordheim theory is used to analyze the electron emission mechanism and operating principle of the device.

articleTitle: Multipactor Dynamics Near a Dielectric Due to Two-Frequency RF Fields
abstract: This work presents time-dependent physics of multipactor discharge on a dielectric surface with transverse rf electric fields of two carrier frequencies, by using a one-dimensional multiparticle Monte Carlo (MC) simulator with adaptive time steps. The study shows that two-frequency operation can reduce the multipactor strength compared to single-frequency operation with the same total rf power. Migration of multipactor trajectory for different configurations of the two-frequency rf field is demonstrated. Surface charging with a small frequency separation between the two carrier modes results in the formation of beat waves in the temporal profiles of the normal electric field. The effect of the frequency separation is not prominent on multipactor susceptibility.

articleTitle: Preparation of boron-doped diamond attenuator for W-band folded waveguide traveling wave tube
abstract: Attenuators with high thermal conductivity and high fracture strength were required in vacuum electronic devices. In this work, boron-doped diamond film which was used as microwave attenuation material was prepared by DC arc jet chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and the boron-doped diamond attenuator for W-band fold waveguide traveling wave tube (TWT) was fabricated based on simulation results. The results showed that the dielectric constant of boron-doped diamond film was between 7.49 and 8.43, and the loss tangent was around 0.32 in W-band. Meanwhile, the fracture strength of boron doped diamond was 428±22 MPa in average. In addition, the voltage standing wave ration (VSWR) and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> of boron doped CVD diamond attenuator were less than 1.10 and below −50 dB in the range of 85–110 GHz.

Author Keywords: W-band folded waveguide traveling wave tube

articleTitle: Research Progress of Pressed Sc2O3 Doped Y-Gd-Hf-O Cathode
abstract: In order to enhance the scandium oxide doped Y-Gd-Hf-O cathodes anti-electron bombardment ability and prolong its lifetime in continuous wave magnetrons, the scandia doped cathode emitters were prepared by a new pressing technique combined with high temperature sintering in hydrogen atmosphere. Surface microstructure and thermionic emission performance of the cathodes were investigated in this abstract.

articleTitle: Design of a TWT Collector Integrable on the same Substrate of a Planar Slow Wave Structure
abstract: In this paper, we report the design of a collector, for a traveling wave tube, that could be realized on a dielectric substrate. The collector could be directly integrated with a planar slow wave structure, such as a meander line, directly on the same substrate. The novel approach could reduce part of the fabrication costs of a TWT. The designed collector can work up to a beam current of 40 mA. Several beam voltages from 5 kV to 10 kV were considered. A maximum collector efficiency of 95.7% was achieved.

articleTitle: An Upgraded 4 Meters Long Traveling Wave Tube for Plasma Physics Research
abstract: We consider a 4 meters long traveling wave tube (TWT) that presents an upgraded slow wave structure. We analyze linear and nonlinear phenomena due to the beam-wave interaction in the device, e.g. beam modulation, and wave growth and saturation.

articleTitle: Investigation of 0.22THz Window for THz Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier
abstract: In this paper, a novel broadband window with diamond piece for 0.22THz traveling wave tube is designed. The two-stage waveguide structure is presented by simulation. The attenuation and VSWR were analyzed by changing the structure size contained the thickness and the diameter of the window disk, the length and the radius of the two-stage waveguide cylindrical waveguide. The simulation results show the attenuation of the window is about -0.2dB during 0.22THz-0.25THz, the VSWR is less than 1.1, which meets the practical requirements in 0.22THz TWT.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of RF-Gun for IAP RAS Photoinjector Accelerator Complex
abstract: The development of an accelerator complex based on the photoinjection gun and designed for the formation of electron bunches with a charge of up to 100 pC and particles energy of ∼ 3 - 5 MeV is currently under way at the IAP RAS. The report presents the design and design parameters of the accelerating microwave section, as well as the results of “cold” testing of its key components.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Correlated Analysis with Material Surface Treatment for Multipactor Suppression of Space Microwave Devices
abstract: Multipactor suppression of space microwave devices is of vitual significance for RF systems operated in vacuum environment, which can prevent the deterioration of device performance. This research presents one multi-scale correlated method of multipactor analysis, which involves the atomic scale of material, the micro morphology scale of device surface and the device scale, is proposed for multipactor suppression and performance improvement of microwave devices. The method is further applied to graphene covered nickel surface in specific device structure and is finally verified by comparing the results of correlated analysis with the experimental measurements, which indicates a promising prospect in space application.

articleTitle: A Compact Mode-selective Attenuator to Suppress High-order Oscillations in Sheet Beam Traveling-wave Tube
abstract: A series of complicated mode competition issues have narrowed the development of sheet beam devices. The high-order mode oscillation problems of a sub-terahertz 220 GHz sheet beam traveling wave tube (SB-TWT) is investigated in this paper. And a compact mode-selective attenuator is presented to suppress the oscillation effectively. Compared with the traditional method of placing attenuation or sever in the middle position of slow-wave structure (SWS), this scheme will not affect the gain of the working mode that is very suitable for applications in the terahertz frequency band.

articleTitle: A Design of a Transverse Magnetic Field Scanning System with 12 Elliptical Coils for Gyrotron Oscillator Collector
abstract: In this abstract, a magnetic field scanning system, composed of 12 transverse elliptical coils and 2 vertical DC coils, has been designed to reduce the peak value and average power of the electron beam on the collector surface. According to the design parameters of the collector of the TE28,8 mode, 140 GHz, 1 MW output power level gyrotron oscillator, the designed results for this scanning system shows that the peak and average power density of the electron beam on the collector surface are not more than 298.66 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 190.94 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, while scanning length reaches 490 mm, which can effectively relieve the pressure of power dissipation and cooling of the collector.

articleTitle: Ultra-High Frequency GaN Nanoscale Vacuum Electronic Devices
abstract: The performances of the GaN nanoscale vacuum electronic devices (NVEDs) were investigated in this paper by theoretical simulation, considering the effects of the device structures. By choosing a proper air channel and aspect ratio, a GaN NVED with a low turn-on voltage and a strong output current can be achieved, showing good agreements with the experiments. The GaN NVED can provide high frequency output in THz band, due to the free transport of electrons in the very small air gap.

articleTitle: Development of a K-band 65-W Space TWT
abstract: This paper describes the development of a K-band space traveling-wave tube (TWT) at the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences (AIRCAS). This K-band space TWT can produce more than 65-W continuous-wave output power and 60% minimum overall efficiency in the operating frequency band. It achieves a compact size less than 260mm (L) x 60mm (W) x 70mm (H) and weighs less than 0.85kg.

articleTitle: A Method for Calculating Electron Inelastic Mean Free Paths with QUANTUM ESPRESSO
abstract: This work aims to propose a method to calculate the inelastic mean free path (IMFP) by means of the energy loss function (ELF) calculated by the density functional theory software “QUANTUM ESPRESSO” (QE). This attempt at IMFP calculations, omitting the intermediate steps of optical energy loss function (OELF) calculations in FPA, and is available to IMFP calculations in the lower energy range. Combined with secondary electron generation model, makes it easier to perform Monte Carlo simulations of secondary electron emission from metals. ELF and IMFP data for Cu and Al crystals in the energy range from 0.1 to 10,000 eV were calculated and compared with the widely used “Full Penn Algorithm” (FPA) results10 with the same trends and orders of magnitude. The secondary electron yield (SEY) simulations are in reasonable agreement with the experimental results.

articleTitle: Microfabrication of 340GHz Folded Waveguide
abstract: A microfabrication process for 340GHz folded waveguide slow-wave structures is developed by using UV-LIGA technology with SU-8 photoresist. The problem of photoresist removal is solved through a hybrid process of liquid chemical dissolving and plasma etching. With optimal process parameters, a 340GHz folded waveguide with high quality is obtained.

articleTitle: Influence of the Aftercavity Interaction on the Output Power of a Gyrotron Operating at a High-Order Axial Mode
abstract: An unexpected abrupt increase of the output power at magnetic field values corresponding to the excitation of high-order axial modes (HOAM) was observed experimentally and is explained theoretically through an after-cavity interaction of the bunched electron beam with the next radial mode. The calculations showed that under certain conditions this effect can be either useful for a power increase at the HOAM operation of the frequency-tunable gyrotron or harmful for high cyclotron harmonic operation due to an expansion of the zone of fundamental cyclotron resonance mode excitation.

articleTitle: Investigation on Algorithm of All-period Optimization of Sheet Beam Traveling-wave Tubes
abstract: To improve the beam-wave interaction efficiency of the sheet beam traveling-wave tubes (SBTWTs), this paper studies the optimization effect of different algorithms on the beam-wave interaction efficiency of staggered double vane (SDV) slow-wave structure (SWS) based on the all-period phase velocity tapering optimization scheme. Through multiple optimization experiments on 30-period SDVSWS, different algorithms are studied to solve the global optimal value of the beam-wave interaction fitness function. By comparison, the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is found to have a strong global search capability and a faster calculation speed. Finally, a 50-period SWS in the Ka-band is designed using PSO algorithm. The beam-wave interaction efficiency is 47.0% calculated by 1-D program and 39.3% verified by particle in cell (PIC) simulation.

articleTitle: Reduction of Ohmic Loss in Terahertz Gyrotrons
abstract: Ohmic loss is one of the essential factors limiting the performance of terahertz gyrotrons. The large dissipated power is attributed to adoption of high Q axial modes (first-order axial mode, FOAM). In this study, we propose a scheme using second-order axial mode (SOAM) to reduce the proportion of ohmic losses. The results show that SOAM has a potential for further improvement of terahertz gyrotron with decreased ohmic losses.

articleTitle: Perturbative analysis of the losses in a TWT
abstract: We present a modified Pierce scheme for small-signal theory of the traveling wave tube, taking into account the losses along the slow wave structure. Moreover, considering attenuation effects as first order perturbation of a lossless TWT, we propose an approximate model for the power output and the overall beam effi-ciency of lossy TWT for different attenuation constant

articleTitle: Plasmon-Enhanced Resonant Photoemission from Metal Surfaces Coated with Ultrathin Dielectric
abstract: In this study, we propose to coat metal nano-emitters with an atomically thick dielectric to further enhance the laser field near the nanotips and therefore the photoemission current. An optical field enhancement factor of up to 400 is demonstrated by the full-wave optical simulation, depending on the geometry of the nano-emitter and resonance wavelengths. A quantum photoemission model, which is constructed by solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, is utilized to investigate the photoemission processes. It is found that, over a wide range of laser fields, the emission current density from the coated photoemitter is enhanced by at least 2 orders of magnitude as compared to the bare emitter. The optical field emission regime can be reached at a much smaller field strength compared to the bare emitter.

articleTitle: Chirping of Gyrotron Radiation in the Process of Raman Backscattering on Electron Beam with Variable Voltage for Subsequent Pulse Compression
abstract: We demonstrate theoretically the possibility of using the regime of Raman backscattering of forward pump wave into the backward propagating signal wave for tuning the radiation frequency. Absolute instability that develops in this system, makes it possible to smoothly change the frequency of the scattered signal when the electron energy changes. According to simulations, with use of 50 kW, 35 GHz gyrotron as a pump wave source considered modulator can generate frequency tunable signal in 3GHz bandwidth with up to 60% conversion efficiency. For subsequent compression of chirped pulse, we suggest to use multi-fold helically corrugated waveguides which allowed us to obtain pulses with peak power up to the 2 MW.

articleTitle: Pumping Systems for Compton FEL-Scattrons: RF-Undulators and Powering Relativistic Masers
abstract: Conception of Compton FEL-scattrons is under development at IAP RAS and aimed at reducing energy of a driving relativistic electron beam, increasing efficiency of the electron-wave interaction and achieving relative compactness of the generator. The basis of pumping system for such type FEL consists of (a) the so-called “flying” undulators, which allow realization of the non-resonant trapping regime when profiling its parameters, and (b) spatially-extended narrow-band sub-GW power Cerenkov masers with 2D distributed feedback implemented in the 2D doubly-periodical slow-wave structures for powering these RF -undulators. Present paper is devoted to the design parameters, results of simulations and current experimental studies of profiled “flying” undulators and powerful radiation sources at the Ka-band.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of Higher-Order Mode Coaxial Type Extended Interaction Cavities for a Ka-Band Multiple Beam Klystron
abstract: This article presents computer aided design and simulation results of intermediate and input/output cavities operating in 2π Mode for a 6-beam Ka band klystron. Coaxial type extended interaction cavities, in which the central conductor was optimized for symmetric field distribution, have been proposed for this multiple beam klystron (MBK). The coaxial cavity configuration with higher order mode allows usage of larger size cavities compared to conventional re-entrant fundamental TM mode cavities. Consequently, more beams can be accommodated and considerable ease in fabrication complexity can be achieved. The proposed MBK may find applications in high data rate mm-wave communication systems, satellite links, 5G wireless backhaul for which Ka band frequencies are becoming increasingly popular.

articleTitle: On-Chip Electron Sources Based on Horizontal Tunneling Junction
abstract: Electron source based on horizontal tunneling junction is an emerging on-chip electron source. It displays balanced emission performances in several important aspects including emission current, emission current density, emission efficiency, switching speed, driving voltage and operating vacuum, which makes it a promising candidate for various on-chip vacuum electronic devices and systems. Herein, the essential results of this novel electron source are summarized.

articleTitle: Megawatt Power Gyrotron with Generation Regimes at the 1st and 2nd Cyclotron Harmonics
abstract: The concept of a gyrotron capable of generating megawatt power in CW or long-pulse regimes with excitation at both the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonics of the gyrofrequency is theoretically developed. For selective excitation at the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> cyclotron harmonic under conditions of a significant excess of the operating current over the threshold, we propose to lock the gyrotron with a weak (several percent in power) monochromatic external signal, which suppresses parasitic oscillations at the fundamental cyclotron resonance in the process of start-up scenario. Based on simulations within the non-stationary self-consistent model, we demonstrate feasibility of a double-frequency gyrotron with an output power of~1 MW at the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> cyclotron harmonic (19 GHz) and ~0.8 MW at the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> one (38 GHz). Such source of radiation is of interest for plasma-heating systems in spherical tokamaks.

articleTitle: Dual-frequency 19 / 38 GHz MW Gyrotron Design for Spherical Tokamak
abstract: In spherical tokamaks, the magnetic field is strongly non-uniform inside the plasma, so the electron-cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) condition is fulfilled only in small volume for fixed microwave frequency. Therefore, for spherical tokamak facilities the plasma heating and confinement regime depends on the position of ECRH area. For this purpose, the gyrotron capable for CW operation with output power of 1 MW at two different frequencies of 19 GHz and 38 GHz is designed.

articleTitle: Q-Band Linearizer for SatCom Applications
abstract: The development, design and test of a Q-band linearizer and channel amplifier to be operated with a travelling wave tube amplifier (TWTA) in satellite communication payloads is summarized in this paper. An overview about the equipment design, development activities, performance and current status of the equipment is provided. Some details concerning the RF line-up and unit functionality are presented and relevant topics from the component development and technology selection are outlined. Finally some performance data are given to illustrate the linearizer capabilities.

articleTitle: Effects of MgO on the sintering and vacuum flashover performance of the chromium and manganese doped Al2O3 ceramics
abstract: The Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ceramics with high flashover voltage were prepared by powder metallurgic method. The surface voltage-withstanding performance of Cr and Mn doped Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ceramic was improved obviously with the addition of small amount of MgO. The crystalline phases were identified by XRD and the microstructures were observed by SEM, the results showed that the addition of MgO could inhibit the grain growth and promote the sintering of Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ceramic. When 0.5 wt.% MgO was added, the Cr and Mn doped Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ceramics had homogeneous microstructure and the vacuum hold-off voltage reached to 24 kV, which was 20 % higher than that without MgO.

articleTitle: Experimental Research of Transparent Cathode
abstract: Theoretical analysis and experiments have been done to evaluate the fast-startup effect of transparent cathode technology. A series of transparent cathode with 30 degree opening angle fan-shaped cross section units have been used in an L-band relativistic magnetron, experimental results shown opposite fast-startup effects between 3-unit transparent cathode and 6-unit scheme. 6-unit transparent cathode advanced the startup process by 4.1 nanoseconds, while 3-unit design caused a startup delay of 0.5 nanosecond. According to electro-static simulation results, transparent cathode has a great impact on the state of electro-static potential gradient distribution, then electron spoke is modulated. Transparent cathodes bring fast startup effect only when the electro-static field is in proper distribution.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of gyrotron radiation frequency multiplication
abstract: We present two sets of experiments on the multiplication of gyrotron radiation frequency. The first one utilizes the second-order susceptibility of the crystal lattice in InP semiconductor with maximum conversion efficiency estimated at 1%. The second experiment is focused on the effect of simultaneous excitation of modes of the cylindrical resonator, resonant with the first, second, and third cyclotron harmonics with the conversion efficiency of up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>.

articleTitle: Development of a Low-Voltage Millimeter-Band Traveling-Wave Tube With a Planar Microstrip Slow-Wave Structure on Dielectric Substrate
abstract: Planar microstrip slow-wave structures (SWS) are suitable for using in miniaturized low-voltage traveling-wave tubes (TWT) with sheet electron beam operating in millimeter-wave band. Such tubes are very promising for application in modern high-data-rate wireless communication systems. In this paper, we present the results of technology development for fabrication of the microstrip SWSs on dielectric substrates, and the results of hot-test numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Influence of Photothermal Effect on Thermal-photon Emission
abstract: In existing cathode thermal-photon emission experiments, it is found that the measured current density/quantum efficiency is significantly higher than the estimated result of Fowler-DuBridge (FdB) equation in the temperature region close to the operating temperature. And till now, this phenomenon still hasn't been well explained. In this paper, we studied the influence of photothermal effect on thermal-photon emission. Simulation results show that the consideration of temperature increase induced by photothermal effect can explain the phenomenon to some extent.

articleTitle: Study on a Broadband Input Power Coupler Component for the W band TE02 mode Gyro-TWT
abstract: A study of a broadband input power coupler component for a W band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode gyro-TWT has been presented. The designed broadband input power coupler component consists of one pillbox window and one Y-type input coupler. By using this, the broadband power drive for the W-band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode gyro-TWT has been achieved. The measurement result indicates that the VSWR of the input coupler component is between 1.13 and 2.5, the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> parameter is less than −3.5dB with the bandwidth of 10GHz, which agrees with the simulation result. In additional, the component has been applied in a sample tube of the W band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode gyro-TWT.

articleTitle: Investigation of 140GHz double-grating extended interaction oscillator
abstract: In this paper, A 140GHz double-grating sheet beam extended interaction oscillator (SB-EIO) is designed. The high- frequency characteristics and transmission characteristics are calculated by a three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation software. The resonant cavity structure is simulated by using the eigenmode solver. And the electric-field distribution satisfies TM110 mode. From the cold cavity simulation results, we can draw the dispersion curve by observing the electric-field distribution under different working modes of the single-period structure. And then, the working frequency of the hot cavity is 143 GHz by combining the voltage line and the dispersion curve's ordinate at 2π working point. With voltage 43.7 kV and current 2.5 A, it can be find that the peak power of output port is 30.11kW, and the beam-wave interaction efficiency is 27.56%.

articleTitle: A Power Divider With Three Octave Bandwidths Based on Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology
abstract: In this paper, the design and measurement of a 6-18 GHz ultra-wideband power divider are presented. Different from conventional hollow waveguide or dielectric transmission line power dividers reported before, the proposed divider adopts the ridge gap waveguide (RGW) for its characters of low insertion loss, broadband, and easy fabrication. The proposed structure consists of a T-junction, a step impedance transformation section, and a pair of 90° RGW bends. In order to suppress the parasitic reactance caused by the discontinuity of transmission line, an inductive iris realized by is introduced at the base block of the RGW. A prototype of the power divider is fabricated and tested. The measured results demonstrate that the return loss of the power divider is better than 15 dB over 100% operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: Simulation design of 2-18GHz ultra-broadband helix traveling-wave tubes
abstract: Broadband traveling-wave tubes (TWTs) commonly have a helix pitch profile which incorporates a section with increased phase velocity followed by a negative phase velocity. To design 2–18 GHz ultra-broadband (UBB) TWT, the second harmonics are saturated output power, based on 3-D large signal software MTSS, are simulated using normal (unloaded T-metal) and abnormal (loaded T-metal) dispersion helix circuits, respectively. It is shown that structures may reduce the generation of the second harmonic while maintaining the high frequency saturated output power. Adding a positive phase velocity taper may further reduce the second harmonics of most frequency points and improve the saturated output power of high frequency band.

articleTitle: Long Term Stability Study of Planar, Two-terminal Field Emitters
abstract: Two different types of planar nano-scale (4–5 nm) field emitters, bowtie and diode devices, were characterized for use as electron sources for vacuum nano-transistors. I-V measurements were performed, and long-term stability tests were conducted in a dedicated life-time test chamber under high vacuum environment (~5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> Torr). Experiments showed that the maximum field emission current was ≈ 3 nA from bowtie devices for a bias voltage of 6 V and ≈ 15 nA from diode devices at a bias voltage of 8 V. A long-term stability study showed that although one diode device failed at ≈300 hr, three other devices emitted a stable current (<5 % Drop) for> 1000 hrs. of continuous operation at a DC bias of 6 V.

articleTitle: High Power Backward Wave Oscillator using Serpentine Waveguide with Distributed Power Extraction Operating at an Exceptional Point
abstract: We show that a backward wave oscillator (BWO) using a millimeter-wave serpentine waveguide, with a degenerate regime of operation based on an exceptional point of degeneracy (EPD), generates very high output power with high efficiency. We introduce distributed power extraction along the serpentine waveguide to satisfy the necessary condition to have an EPD. Particle in cell (PIC) simulation results show self-standing oscil-lations at 90 GHz with an improvement in output power level, approximately 40 times higher, and with improved efficiency of 15% rather than 1% of a standard millimeter-wave BWO.

articleTitle: Development and Application of Emission Models in the MICHELLE Beam Optics Simulation Code
abstract: We present new advances in the MICHELLE charged particle beam optics code in area of advancing emission models and algorithms that capture more electron emission physics. The new capability covered in this paper concerns the implementation of a new general thermal field (GTF) model that predicts current density in the transition region between temperature limited emission and field emission. In the case of electron thermionic emission where the effective AK gap is not large compared with the potential minimum distance that forms in front of the cathode, we employed a modified and improved thermionic emission model Coupled to these models are a new thermal beam model that better control macro-particle count while maintaining simulation fidelity, as well as new meshing methodologies that improve emission fidelity in the regime of disparate spatial scales, especially useful for field emitter fibers. Lastly, also for field emission fibers, we will present results from the implementation of a self-consistent thermal model. To support such widely ranging spatial scales, effort has been put into disparate meshing capabilities. The presentation provides an overview of the new capabilities that has been achieved.

articleTitle: Direct Coupled Gyrotrons for Plasma Heating
abstract: High power gyrotrons typically produce RF power in a Gaussian free-space mode. An internal converter transforms the whispering gallery mode from the cavity to a Gaussian beam using a quasi-optical launcher and a series of mirrors. Transmission of this power typically requires transformation into an HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode in corrugated waveguide. This conversion is achieved using a Mirror Optical Unit, which uses a second series of mirrors. The transformation of the whispering gallery mode to a Gaussian beam and then to an HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode requires a complexity of RF structures, increasing cost and RF losses. This program is developing a coupler that transforms the whispering gallery mode into an HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode inside the gyrotron. This results in significant reduction in gyrotron cost and RF losses and eliminates the Mirror Optical Unit.

articleTitle: Oversized Waveguide Circular Polarizer for High Power Transmission System
abstract: In this article, a corrugated square waveguide circular polarizer operating from 7 GHz to 10 GHz for gyrotron traveling wave tube application system is proposed. In order to obtain a flat phase difference between two orthogonal linear polarizations, an oversized quasi-square waveguide with corrugations is used. By optimizing the size of the corrugation and the dimension of the waveguide, the different effects on two linear polarizations are obtained, which means the circular polarized wave can be achieved in a broadband. The results show that in the frequency range from 7 GHz to 10 GHz, the relative bandwidth is about 35.3%. The phase difference is about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90\pm 2$</tex> degree.

articleTitle: Vibration Simulation of Microwave Tubes Considering Contact Constraint
abstract: Today, the vibration analysis technology for individual parts or structural components has matured, and its analysis results and calculation accuracy can fully meet the needs of the actual project. However, the structures of microwave tubes are assembled from more than a hundred components. The general rigid connection without considering contact can result in poor solution accuracy. Therefore, it is necessary to consider the connection relationships between components. In this paper, unlike the rigid connection without considering contact, authors use the finite element penalty function method to introduce the bonded contact constraint into the finite element equation while increasing the accuracy of the final analysis results. Through the simulation of microwave tubes, the proposed method has been validated against ANSYS. It has been shown that the proposed method has the same accuracy as ANSYS.

articleTitle: ICEPIC and CST-PS simulations of a “cooker” 2.45 GHz magnetron
abstract: Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of a conventional microwave oven 2.45 GHz “cooker” magnetron with a “cold” explosive-emission cathode and external uniform axial magnetic field 0.19 T are performed with two computer codes, ICEPIC and CST-PS. PIC simulations are done to compare results obtained by these two codes to each other and, by such a way, identify all possible advantages and disadvantages of each code performance as a reliable tool allowing to predict all important characteristics of the magnetron operation. Results of the PIC simulations showed that the range of applied voltages within which the magnetron is able to operate in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex>-mode is much broader inside CST-PS virtual reality (VR), from 4.00 kV to 4.70 kV, than it is inside ICEPIC one, from 3.90 kV to 4.10 kV. It is also shown that while the ICEPIC magnetron startup time gradually decreases from about 700 ns (3.90 kV) to about 100 ns (4.20 kV) with the applied voltage increase, the CST-PS’ one is at first chaotically varies between about 1000 ns (4.03 kV) and about 300 ns (4.01 kV) and only then gradually and rapidly decreases down to almost 10–20 ns (4.40-4.60 kV) with the applied voltage increase. Subjective interpretation of the obtained PIC simulation results suggests that the ICEPIC code would be a quite more reliable tool to deal with in further execution of the planned 2.45 GHz “cooker” magnetron scope of work. Additional PIC simulation with, for example, MAGIC or VORPAL codes, would be interesting to perform as well to clarify the obtained discrepancies in the obtained so far PIC simulation results.

articleTitle: Long-Periodic Cusped Magnet System for Planar-Distributed Multiple Beam Focusing
abstract: In this paper, a planar-distributed three-beam gun with Long-Periodic Cusped Magnet (LPCM) focusing system is presented, and the three-beam electron gun is designed and optimized to get desired model. With proper optimization a beam radius of 0.08 mm is obtained with beam current of 3×0.15 A and voltage of 22 kV. The beam compression factor is 5 for the 0.18 mm beam tunnel radius, and the axis separation of the adjacent electron beams is 0.46 mm. Long-Periodic Cusped Magnet focusing system consisting of permanent magnets and pole pieces have been used for transporting the three-beam. The simulation results show that the three-beam electron gun match well with Long-Periodic Cusped Magnet focusing system, and the three-beam array can transmit 45 mm more stable.

articleTitle: Exact Analytical Theory for Pulsed Laser Induced Photoelectron Emission from Biased Surfaces
abstract: We construct an exact analytical theory for ultrafast photoelectron emission from a dc-biased surface driven by laser pulses, by solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation. The single formulation is valid from photon-driven electron emission in low intensity optical fields to field-driven emission in high intensity optical fields. Our results show the coherent interaction of neighboring laser pulses on the photoemission, and recover the experimentally measured vanishing carrier-envelope-phase sensitivity accompanied by a π phase shift in the optical-field regime. We also find adding a large dc field to the photoemitter is able to greatly enhance the photoemission current and shorten the electron emission pulse.

articleTitle: Design of gyrotron filament power supply based on Buck voltage-fed full-bridge inverter
abstract: Aiming at requirements of gyrotron filament power supply, an adjustable stable current filament power supply is designed with Buck voltage feedback full-bridge inverse topology. The overall design structure of filament power supply and calculation process of important parameters are described in detail. In order to realize the fast tracking of reference signal by the power output, the stability of the system is analyzed through MATLAB and transfer function of the topology. The experimental simulation analysis with PSPICE was carried out and the gyrotron filament power supply satisfying the design requirements was obtained.

articleTitle: Electron Gun with High Compression Ratio for a W-Band Sheet-Beam TWT
abstract: A sheet-beam electron gun with high compression ratio and long transmission distance performance is presented. The operational voltage is set as 30 kV, the beam current is 0.505A and the corresponding cathode loading current density is about 5.59 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The simulation results show that the compression ratio of the obtained sheet beam is over 35 and the transmission rate can reach 100% through a 126 mm beam tunnel using a permanent magnetic focusing system.

articleTitle: RF characterization of integrated gun-cavity for UHF band Inductive Output Tube
abstract: The paper presents simulations and experimental results of radial reentrant cavity employed in Inductive Output Tubes (IOT) for broadcasting and accelerator applications. CST and SUPERFISH software are used for structure designing and are experimentally validated using Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). Since the cavity in IOT, works as a part of electron gun as well, therefore, presented cavity is designed and developed as a conjoined structure of gun cum cavity for a 350 MHz IOT.

articleTitle: Emission Performance of Graphene-Coated Ba-W Cathode
abstract: Emission performance of cathode depends largely on its surface state in terms of work function. By coating or doping appropriate materials on top of the cathode surface, cathode work function can be reduced and emission capability improved. We proposed and fabricated a new type of graphene-coated Ba-W cathode with the measured emission performance presented in this paper. The emission current of the cathode was measured with respect to voltage. And the equivalent surface work function of the cathode obtained using Schottky plot and Richardson plot, is as low as 1.16eV, and at least smaller than 1.56eV, which is significantly lower than that of B-type cathode. This low work function demonstrates the possibility for the cathode to be used as a kind of large current density or low working temperature cathode. However, uniformity and stability of the cathode still needs to be improved, for it was found that only a small part of the surface has participated in the electron emission in low temperature regions.

articleTitle: Transverse Radiation Output for Relativistic Sub-Terahertz Surface-Wave Oscillators
abstract: To organize the output of the radiation for relativistic high-power surface-wave oscillators, we propose using additional diffraction grating with a period twice larger than the period of the main corrugation. This grating scatters the evanescent operating wave into the Gaussian beam propagating perpendicular to grating surface. At the sub-terahertz frequencies, the proposed transverse energy extraction reduces the Ohmic losses drastically thus increasing the device efficiency. According to simulations, surface-wave oscillator based on sheet electron beam with voltage of 600 kV and current of 600 A can provide 90 MW of output power with 25 % efficiency at 150-GHz.

articleTitle: The Design and Optimization for a V-Band Magnetron Injection Gun
abstract: Gyro-travelling-wave-tubes (Gyro-TWT) is a kind of high-power amplifier of vacuum electron device. Magnetron Injection Guns (MIG) is an essential component of Gyro-travelling-wave-tubes. In this paper, a single anode MIG is designed and optimized with genetic algorithm, which electron beam with a pitch ratio of 1.27 and low transverse velocity spread of 1.97% is obtained. The influence of the mismatching relationship between electric and magnetic field on velocity spread is analyzed.

articleTitle: The Importance of Patch Fields in Accurately Modeling Miram Curves
abstract: We develop a model of the non-uniform thermionic emission from spatially heterogeneous cathode surfaces in a parallel diode, including both 3-D space charge and patch field effects. This model is able to predict both the temperature-limited (TL) emission and the full-space-charge-limited (FSCL) emission, as well as the TL-FSCL transition, i.e. the so-called “knee” in the Miram (current density vs. temperature) curve. The modeling results indicate that a thermionic cathode with a spatial distribution of work functions will have a smooth TL-FSCL transition as a result of both the 3-D space charge and patch field effects, even if the work function values are discrete-valued. Such behavior of a smooth Miram curve knee is in agreement with experimental results. This model provides a more physical method to modeling thermionic emission from heterogeneous surfaces. This model helps to understand the insight of emission physics, cathode development, and the design of vacuum electronic devices.

articleTitle: An Accurate Measure Method of Loss Power for Space TWT
abstract: An accurate measuring method of loss power for RF circuit and collector for space TWT is proposed in this paper, which based on the measurement of energy distribution curve at entrance of collector. The method measures the energy distribution curve of collector inlet, the DC power of electron beam, the interception loss power, and the voltage and current of collector. By using the measured energy distribution curve of collector with 10% working ratio, the power in spent beams at entrance of collector can be obtained. Then according to the principle of energy conservation, the circuit loss and the heat loss of the collector can be calculated. A space TWT with a four-stage depressed collector is measured in this paper. Measurement results show that the circuit loss and heat loss of the collector are 1.25W and 45.16W, respectively.

articleTitle: Free-electron-driven vortex beam generator based on compound helical grating
abstract: A free-electron-driven vortex beam emitter based on coherent Smith-Purcell radiation (SPR) induced by the compound helical grating is proposed in this paper. Due to the diffraction of the helical periodic system, vortex beams carrying orbital angular momentum are excited when the ring-shaped electron beam flies over the surface of the grating. The dispersion relations of the uniform and the compound helical grating are analyzed. Owing to the periodic modulating of grating width, the dispersion line of the fundamental mode of the uniform helical grating is split to the fast wave region regarding the Brillouin-band folding phenomenon, and the generated SPR vortex beam is coherent accordingly.

articleTitle: Formation of Microwave Soliton Trains due to Modulation Instability under Cyclotron Resonance Interaction of an Initially Rectilinear Electron Beam with a Backward Electromagnetic Wave
abstract: It is known that under the resonant interaction of a moving beam of unexcited electron cyclotron oscillators with a backward electromagnetic wave, conversion of a continuous-wave (CW) signal into a sequence of short soliton-like pulses may occur. In this paper, this phenomenon is explained based on the theoretical study of the modulation instability (MI). The analysis shows the possibility of implementing several dynamic regimes depending on the amplitude and frequency of the input harmonic signal.
