Analytical expressions for the threshold values of the driving power and frequency required for the soliton generation are derived and compared with the results of numerical simulation. The results of the experimental study of soliton formation are also discussed.

articleTitle: Two-Stage 0.34 THz Sine Waveguide Slow Wave Structure
abstract: Considering the feasibility of manufacturing 0.34THz traveling wave tube (TWT), this paper proposes a new two-seg-ment sine waveguide slow-wave structure (SWS). Unlike the con-ventional sine wave waveguide, a round beam tunnel is used in this modified structure. In order to increase the output power while reducing the impact of reflected signal, this structure adopts the two-stage structure and the phase velocity jump technology. Attenuators are considered here to absorb the reflected signal in the new SWS. The simulation results show that the new structure has the advantages of machinability, wide bandwidth and high gain. Through PIC simulation, for a 54 mm long slow-wave circuit, with an input power of 8 mw, the gain of the new structure is greater than 31 dB and the output power is above 10W in the 0.325-0.355 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: EIO based on Smith-Purcell radiation design operating in high-order mode
abstract: This paper proposes a structure based on Smith-Purcell radiation (SPR) for the design of Extended interaction oscillator(EIO) opreating in high-order mode. Simulation results show that the maximum output power of the EIO can reach 800W at 129 GHz, when the electron beam voltage and current are 38 kV and 0.5A.

articleTitle: Microwave CPA-Amplifier with Multi-Gigawatt Ultrashort Output Pulses
abstract: The possibility of efficient amplification of ultrashort microwave superradiant pulses with use of Chirped Pulse Amplification (CPA) technique had been studied theoretically. This technique implies preliminary stretching of initial pulse, subsequent amplification of chirped pulse with reduced peak power and restoration of pulse original shape in compressor. According to calculations, considered CPA scheme comprising a relativistic Cherenkov amplifier and five-fold helically corrugated oversized waveguides as stretcher and compressor can amplify 30 GHz, 360 ps, 400 MW initial supperradiance pulse up to 8 GW. Thus, the peak power of amplified pulse can exceed power of used electron beam by factor of 4.

articleTitle: CAST Xi'an Q-Band TWTA for high-throughput satellites
abstract: Based on the need of GEO and LEO high-throughput satellites, CAST Xi'an is developing the Q-band TWTA and LTWTA. The space-flight qualification 45-watt Q-band TWTA was completed in 2017, which was applied on “Shijian-20” satellite, a high-throughput communication test satellite, launched in December 2019. Subsequently, CAST Xi'an carried out the development of 80-watt Q-band LTWTA and integrated Q-band power components for LEO satellites.

articleTitle: Design of Truncated Sine-waveguide Structure for THz TWT
abstract: A novel truncated Sine-waveguide Travelling Wave Tube (SWGTWT) is studied to operate in 600–700 GHz. The cold circuit parameters like dispersion diagram, interaction impedance, and phase velocity are obtained. The extent of truncation is optimized to flatten the dispersion curve and to have a reasonable space for beam transportation. PIC simulation is carried out to study high-power oneration.

articleTitle: Prediction model of the parasitic parameters for planar transformer based on extra-trees
abstract: Planar transformer is one of the key technologies for miniaturization of Electronic Power Conditioner used in Travelling-Wave Tube Amplifier. The parasitic parameters for planar transformer are difficult to model because of the nonlinear and multivariable characteristics. This paper presents a prediction model of the parasitic parameters based on the binary particle swarm optimization extra-trees. The model has been trained and verified by the data set of planar transformer. The prediction results confirm the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: Complicated cavities for high-harmonic gyrotrons
abstract: We review our works aimed at creating high-harmonic gyrotrons with cavities of complicated shapes as a way to increase efficiencies of their operation and to improve their selective properties. These works are mainly aimed at the implementation of the large-orbit gyrotrons developed at our Institute on the basis of two experimental installations. At the same time, some approaches have proved attractive also for traditional gyrotron configurations.

articleTitle: A 3.7kV TWTA High Voltage Power Converter Based on LLC
abstract: In this paper, a high voltage LLC resonant half bridge converter with six-segmented rectifier has been designed, which makes MOSEFTEs Zero-Voltage-Switching (ZVS) and rectifier diodes Zero-Current-Switching (ZCS) by using clamping diodes on the splitting resonant for over current protection. The designed converter can provide 3.7kV output voltage with the output efficiency of over 96.00%.

articleTitle: A W-Band Radial Klystron Amplifier
abstract: A W-band klystron amplifier with three-gap radial extended interaction cavity is proposed. The structure consists of an input-cavity, two idle-cavities and an output-cavity, all of which are three-gap radial extended interaction cavities. The field distribution characteristics of the three-gap extended interaction cavity have been studied. The PIC simulation results show that the average output power of the structure is 623W, corresponding a gain of 35.7 dB and an electron efficiency of 5.2% at 94.03GHz, where a radial electron beam (15kV, 0.8A) and 0.6T radial focusing magnetic field are applied.

articleTitle: Relativistic Sub-THz Surface-Wave Oscillators Based on Oversized Cylindrical Waveguides (Quasi-Optical Theory)
abstract: - Within the quasi-optical approach, we investigate the dynamic of excitation of azimuthally-symmetric TM modes in a relativistic surface-wave oscillator (SWO) with oversized cylindrical waveguide. We outline the two operation regimes, namely, the n-mode excitation regime and the regime of backward surface wave oscillator. Based on theoretical considerations, we demonstrate the viability of practical realization of relativistic SWS with a power level of up to 100 MW in the sub-THz wavelength band.

articleTitle: The copper plating technology of 1.3 GHz Fundamental Power Input Coupler
abstract: The copper plating technology on the cold coax and worm coax of the coupler was studied, including design the plastic mold to prevent the outer wall of coupler from being electroplated with copper film. The copper film obtained by electroplating process was compact and had no porosity. The surface permeability and the residual resistivity ratio was discussed. Moreover, the binding force of copper film and matrix had been tested, which was used high pressure water spraying at 8.5 MPa for 10 min, liquid nitrogen and worm water at 95°C alternately impinged, stretched and compressed the bellows for 10 mm. After the binding force tests, the copper film of the coupler was observed by endoscope to find that there was not particle detachment and peeling.

articleTitle: Spontaneous Coherent Super-Radiative Emission of Ultra-Short Terahertz Wave Pulse
abstract: We study spontaneous coherent super-radiative undulator emission in the Terahertz frequency range from a short dense electron bunch. Since the group velocity of the radiated wave coincides with the bunch velocity, this is a process of the spontaneous radiation and, then, amplification of a single wave cycle. As a result, formation of an ultra-short (several cycles) wave packet occurs. Since the radiated field prevents the destruction of the bunch under the influence of its own Coulomb fields, the process of effective spontaneous coherent radiation is maintained for a relatively long length of the electron-wave interaction region. In the optimized system, this results in a high (10-15%) efficiency of the radiation process, as well as in a high intensity (several hundred MV/m) of the field accommodated in the short wave packet.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of a 300 GHz Folded Waveguide Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: The design and experimental results of a 300 GHz folded waveguide traveling-wave tube (TWT) are presented. The folded waveguide was designed for operation with a 10.8 kV electron beam and fabricated using a nano-CNC machine. From the simulation results the gain of the designed TWT is approximately 35 dB. Sever wedges were designed and fabricated using Ceradyne Ceralloy 137CD-1 which was tested using quasi-optical measurement system. The pillbox type RF window was designed, fabricated, and tested. The performance of the electron gun was evaluated; beam current is higher than 100 mA at beam voltage of 11 kV. More experiments are under progress.

articleTitle: Research of New Type of Resonant Microwave Pulse Compression System with 3-E-T Power Combiner
abstract: In this paper, a new physical model of the resonant microwave pulse compression is proposed. In the new model, opposite to the traditional theory and technology, the branch-output waveguide are set at the peak of the standing wave of the microwave resonant cavity, rather than at the node as in traditional model. The simulation results shown that, for the rectangular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode in the over-sizeded microwave resonant cavity, the following requirements of the energy-coupling coefficient ßs=0.5, the TW-power gain G=120, and the combined peak power P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>=480MW/3.5ns can be realized at 2.92GHz, when the cavity is driven by an advanced high-power klystron with input of IMW/2.92GHz/50µs.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a High-Power 48GHz Gyroklystron Amplifier for Accelerator Applications
abstract: A 48GHz gyroklystron amplifier has been designed using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation techniques. The beam is provided by a magnetron injection gun (MIG). The gyroklystron is predicted to deliver 2MW of output power at 48GHz with a gain of 35dB and an efficiency of 38%. The design was developed with consideration of the harmonic linearizer of a linear accelerator (linac) that is being designed as part of the H2020 CompactLight X-ray free electron laser (XFEL) project.

articleTitle: An Ultra-broadband Metamaterial Absorber Based on the Square Split Ring
abstract: An ultra-broadband metamaterial absorber (MA) is proposed in this paper. It is composed of a three-layer structure: one dielectric medium between two metal inserts. The simulation result shows that the bandwidth of this metamaterial absorber is about 55 GHz from 91.13 GHz to 146.13 GHz when the absorptivity achieves 0.99. The relative bandwidth ratio is 46%. This MA can be easily fabricated by surface micro-machining technology.

articleTitle: A Novel Meander Line SWS for Low Voltage and High Efficiency Ka-Band TWT
abstract: A novel meander line slow-wave structure (ML-SWS) based on a series of concentric arcs was proposed for applications on low voltage and high efficiency Ka-band traveling-wave tube (TWT). The simulated results demonstrate that the proposed novel ML-SWS has a good transmission performance in Ka-band. The peak output power of the TWT can reach 60.1 W at 35 GHz. The corresponding gain and the electron efficiency is 22.2 dB and 41.71%, respectively. Furthermore, the 3-dB bandwidth can cover 25 GHz-44 GHz and the electron efficiency is over 26.8% in Ka-band.

articleTitle: Design of a Tunable 400-GHz Second-Harmonic Gyrotron with Selective Grooves
abstract: A design of a cryomagnet-based second-harmonic gyrotron is proposed, in which a special profile of an axisymmet-ric cavity is used for efficient discrimination of the fundamental-harmonic mode in a wide range of operating magnetic fields and for providing a wide band of the frequency tuning when operating in several axial modes. According to simulations, for the beam voltage of 15 kV it is possible to achieve a frequency tuning of up to 0.3% when operating at several axial modes near the frequency of 400 GHz with an output power of at least 10 W. This design is to be implemented on the base of 8 T cryomagnet at the FIR Center, Fukui.

articleTitle: High Gain Double Gate Vacuum Emission Transistor with low Leakage Current
abstract: A double-gate vacuum field emission transistor array (DG-VFETA) is presented in this paper, which design the gate structure to eliminates gate leakage current caused by particle beam. This is verified by the particle trajectory simulated by CST. The simulation results also indicate that the cut-off frequency of the device can be reached to 3.97 THz This DG-VFETA consists of 1000 emitters, which has a 24.3 dB power gain with an input signal at 10 V amplitude and 200 mA. This shows a potential application of DG-VFETA as an amplifier in THz regime.

articleTitle: Design of a High Compression Ratio Electron Gun for Terahertz TWT Applications
abstract: The design of a high compression ratio electron gun has been discussed, which is intended for a 0.22 THz traveling wave tube amplifier. The circular beam electron gun is simulated by means of CST particle studio to determine the electron beam trajectory. The simulation results predict that the designed electron gun produces a circular beam with the waist radius of 0.054 mm, corresponding to the beam voltage of 21.3 kV and the beam current of 61.5 mA.

articleTitle: System Design of Orbital Angular Momentum Transmitter Using Dual-Beam Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier
abstract: As a breakthrough technology for achieving high spectrum efficiency in millimeter-wave wireless communications, vortex beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) have attracted much attention. However, due to high divergence of OAM beam in free space, which is an inherent property of the OAM beams, possible wireless communication distance is restricted, and bulkier receiver system configuration is inevitable as communication distance increases. Hence, we try to overcome the issues with two approaches that can extend the wireless communication coverage. The one is high-directivity OAM antenna design and the other is use of a dual-beam traveling wave tube amplifier for securing high signal-to-noise ratio. The OAM antenna consists of a nonlinear taper and a lens-integrated metamaterial structure for a low divergence angle. A proposed transmitter system may contribute for realizing millimeter-wave OAM wireless communications. The details will be provided in the paper.

articleTitle: Frequency Tuning Characteristic of a Sub-THz Quasi-Optical Gyrotron Cavity by Mirror Separation Adjusting
abstract: A high-power frequency-tunable sub-THz quasi-optical gyrotron cavity based on confocal waveguide is designed in this paper. The frequency tuning characteristic of the cavity has been investigated by Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulation. Results predict that the oscillation frequency of the proposed quasi-optical cavity could be tuned in a range of 17.1 GHz around 0.22 THz by only adjusting the mirror separation distance. Moreover, combining the adjustments of mirror separation and magnetic field, a smoothly continuous frequency tuning band with an extraordinarily broad bandwidth of 41.5 GHz can be obtained, corresponding to a relative bandwidth of 18.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> to the center frequency 0.22THz. Meanwhile the output power keeps no less than 20 kW during the hybrid adjustment. Quasi-optical gyrotron cavity performs a good frequency tunability and may be conducive for developing the high-power frequency-tunable THz gyrotron oscillators.

articleTitle: Parallel implementation of space charge force calculation in SUNRAY-1D using MPI
abstract: SUNRAY-1D is a one-dimensional large signal code for analyzing the beam-wave interaction in helix traveling wave tubes (TWTs). In order to improve the performance of SUNRAY-1D, parallelization of few of its modules has been initiated. Parallel implementation of space charge force module using MPI (message passing interface) has been successful. Improvements, in terms of increased accuracy and reduced computational time, have been the key benefits achieved.

articleTitle: Powerful W-band Planar Cherenkov Maser: Design, Simulations and State of Experiments
abstract: Project of sub-GW to GW power W-band planar Cherenkov oscillator driven by large-size sheet electron beam forming by the “ELMI” accelerator 1 MeV / 7 kA / 3 µs is under development in collaboration between IAP RAS (N.Novgorod) and BINP RAS (Novosibirsk). Electrodynamic system of this maser is based on 2D periodical slow-wave structure realizing 2D distributed feedback mechanism and allowing for provision of stable narrow-band oscillation regime under conditions of substantial oversize. Design parameters, key components and results of simulations of this oscillator are presented, status of its experimental realization is discussed.

articleTitle: Circuit Design of a Broadband W-Band Extended Interaction Klystron
abstract: A novel circuit with broad bandwidth is designed for the W-band Extended Interaction Klystron (EIK) in this paper. The three operating modes (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex> mode, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi+1$</tex> mode, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi+2$</tex> mode) with a certain frequency interval among them are analyzed, which results in expanding bandwidth of the circuit. The circuit is powered under condition of a 2A, 2. 7kV pencil beam with 0.2mm radius and 11mm EIK circuit length, whose simulation results predict that the saturated output power is 91 0W and 3dB bandwidth is greater than 750 MHz.

articleTitle: Research on a 6-18GHz High Power Helix Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: A helix traveling wave tube(TWT) with a support rod embedded in a metal block operating at 6–18 GHz is proposed in this paper. The pitch and the radius of the helix are gradually changed or jumped to suppress the second harmonic and obtain high power output. The output power of the high-power helix TWT can be more than 5 kW, except for the sharp decrease at 6 GHz that reaches 3.59 kW.

articleTitle: Research on Improved High Efficiency Optimization Method for SBEIO
abstract: This paper improves the design method for optimizing the sheet beam extended interaction oscillator (SBEIO) based on the simulated annealing algorithm. This optimization method combines the correlation analysis of the SBEIO electric field distribution with an improved non-linear calculation program to optimize the 9-gaps SBEIO. By performing a correlation analysis on the electric field distribution trend of the extended interaction oscillator and finding the constraint relationship between the electric field amplitude coefficients, the optimization step can be simplified. And improved the MATLAB program for non-linear theoretical calculation. The efficiency of 64 electronic calculations only took 13.68s, which is 10 times higher than before. At the same time, after the output power curve has stabilized, the fluctuation is only 0.128%. The efficiency from the non-linear calculation program are up to 19.03%.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-beam Magnetron Injection Gun for W-band Gyro-TWT
abstract: In order to enhance the power capacity of Gyro-TWT in high frequency, a novel multi-sector-tunnel Gyro-TWT is study in this paper. The multi-sector-tunnel could extend the transverse dimension of RF circuit for higher power electron transmission. The azimuthal drift performance of cyclotron electron was discussed and a multi-beam magnetron injection gun (MIG) is design. An electron beam with pitch factor of 1.02 and axial velocity spread of 2.98% is obtained.

articleTitle: Compass Framework Multidisciplinary System Design Optimization (MSDO) Applications
abstract: The Compass framework manages simulation pipelines. Any simulation software can be mapped into a Compass compatible module using Compass' module template. Once-developed modules can be reused for other simulation pipelines with little additional effort. The Compass module interface is designed so that modules can communicate data between each other with the only requirement being that the data transferred is of the same data type in both modules. The Compass framework is discussed. Application of the Compass framework to multidisciplinary problems is presented.

articleTitle: A 81-86GHz TWTA For Wireless Communication
abstract: BVERI has being developing a CW E-band traveling wave tube amplifier (TWTA) for high speed wireless communications applications. The TWTA integrates a folded waveguide CW TWT and a modular electronic power conditioner (EPC), with operating frequency range from 81 to 86GHz, capable of saturated output power over 80W and 22% overall efficiency. The combination test results of TWTA and predistortion linearizer shows that the 1dB compressed point output (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</inf>) and the third-order intermodulation ratio (IMD3) have been distinctly improved.

articleTitle: Recent results of 0.5 terahertz gyrotrons with record power
abstract: Two 0.5 THz gyrotrons were successfully tested at IAP RAS, Russia: 0.526 THz/240 W continuous and 0.53 THz / 200 kW pulsed (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20 \ \mu\mathrm{s}$</tex>). Both tubes demonstrate quite high power in their class. Continuous gyrotron operates on second cyclotron harmonic with maximum power of 240 W (with efficiency about 2.8%) at beam current of 600 mA and accelerating voltage of 15 kV. It is also capable of operating in low-power regime with beam current al low as 20 mA. Pulsed gyrotron has about 20T magnetic field to operate on first-harmonic TE23.7 mode. Due to small average power of output radiation (about 4 J), the calorimetric measurements were carried out using 3D-printed dummy load with tiny water stream volume and thermally insulated internal boundary, which provided sufficient temperature difference between inlet and outlet fluid to measure the power in a single pulse mode. Experimental results open new perspectives of using such sources in advanced spectroscopic science, such as DNP/NMR and EPR, where both high frequency and high-power microwave radiation are needed. The unique combination of the output parameters of the CW gyrotron made it possible, in particular, to efficiently heat materials for the production of highly dispersed powders of metal oxides by evaporation-condensation method.

articleTitle: Simulation and Design of 300 GHz CW Clinotron Oscillator on Hybrid Surface-Volume Modes
abstract: The results of the research and design of a new model of clinotron with the non-uniform grating structure. The tube is designed to operate at the several regimes those are promising for efficient excitation of the THz waves. The regime of the hybrid surface-volume mode is considered numerically. The design of the clinotron contains two power outputs: the backward wave (BW) output and the space wave (SW) output. The simulation results demonstrate double magnification of the output power at the SW output compared to the BW output. The experimental prototype of the clinotron has been designed and manufactured according to the simulation results.

articleTitle: A Critical Examination of Induced Current on Conductors Due to a Moving Line Charge
abstract: The classical Ramo-Shockley theorem gives the induced current on a conductor, assuming quasi-static motion of charges and electrostatic fields. This paper presents examples of the induced current distribution that is relativistically and electromagnetically correct.

articleTitle: Field emission from dielectric coated metallic cathode surfaces: a theoretical study
abstract: In this paper, we develop an exact analytical theory for field emission from dielectric-coated metallic cathode surfaces, by solving the one-dimensional (1D) time-independent Schrödinger equation subject to a double-triangular barrier. The theory includes the effects of cathode properties (work function and Fermi energy), dielectric properties (thickness, dielectric constant, and electron affinity), and applied dc electric field. Our results show that the emission current density from cathodes in certain coating conditions is larger than the bare case. An empirical relation between the threshold dielectric thickness and threshold dielectric constant is given. This work provides insights for designing field emitters of higher efficiency and better stability.

articleTitle: G-band phase-velocity-taper Traveling Wave Tube Based On Quasi Flat-roofed Sine Waveguide
abstract: A G-band phase-velocity-taper quasi flat-roofed sine waveguide traveling wave tube (TWT) with sheet electron beam is proposed to amplify the millimeter wave. In this paper, the PIC method is used to obtain the interaction characteristics of the sheet electron beam and the electromagnetic wave in this structure. We reduce the phase velocity by reducing the oscillating period, the calculation results indicate that the traveling wave tube can produce over 205 W output power and 33 dB gain at the center frequency 220 GHz, the gain is greater than 31 dB from 215 GHz to 225 GHz and the maximum electronic efficiency is 4.5%, The calculation also show that the output power at 220 GHz can increased 49% compared with the without-taper structure, the corresponding electron efficiency is improved from 3.0% to 4.5% by phase-velocity-taper.

articleTitle: An IGBT Drive Circuit Controlled By Synchronous Signal Based On Magnetic Coupling Technology
abstract: This paper describes an IGBT drive circuit based on a synchronous signal control based on magnetic coupling technology. The drive circuit integrates the advantages of magnetic coupling technology, and strengthens the controllability of this coupling method by improving the secondary loop. In this way, the volume of the high-voltage pulse generator can be more compact and more stable. Through experiments, the superiority of this method is confirmed.

articleTitle: The Hot Test of A High Average Power Broadband Ka-Band Sheet Beam Traveling-wave Tube
abstract: Progress on a more than 2 kW average power and 50% working duty broadband Ka-band sheet beam traveling-wave tube (SB- TWT) is reported for the first time. Overall device has been designed, fabricated, and tested in UESTC. The TWT employs a periodic cusp magnet (PCM) focusing system allowing above 95% transmission and compact package. The unsaturated measured peak output power exceeds 4 kW with over 50% duty corresponding 26.7 dB gain and 31.9% efficiency at 28 GHz with single-stage collector depression. The 3-dB bandwidth is 7 GHz from 26 GHz to 33 GHz under the unsaturated driven. The details of the experiment are discussed.

articleTitle: The Wideband Mini- TWT For T/R Module Applications
abstract: This paper describes the wideband mini- TWT development and manufacture of 64-elements T/R modules for phased array applications. The output peak power of module reached 350W with 20% duty cycle over the X-Ku band. The module cross section dimensions were 130mm X 22mm which suitable for phased array radar T/R module with four horn connected with one module.

articleTitle: Photoemission Assisted by Low workfunction Nanoparticle Waveguide Integrated Device
abstract: Photoemission has been spotlighted due to its wide usages in free electron laser source and vacuum electronic high-power devices. Photon assisted electron emitter is typically limited by i) low quantum efficiency and ii) high work function of the emitter. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid photoemitter using a lanthanum hexaboride (LaB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>) nanoparticle on single layer graphene assisted by waveguide structure to pass through these challenges. LaB6 nanoparticle, which has low work function (2.69eV) is an ideal material for electron emission purposes due to its miniature dimensions, as well as excellent electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties. By integrating LaB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> on top of graphene with waveguide we could evanescent coupling occurs through longer interaction length and photons can be absorbed efficiently compared to free space laser illumination. In addition, nanoparticles with the average diameter of 4 nm are at the order of electron mean free path and electron emission occurs with fewer scattering compared to electron emission from bulky metallic emitters. Hybrid photoemitter can open a new pathway towards realizing high power devices for commercial usage.

articleTitle: Modeling and Interface Engineering of Electrical Contacts
abstract: Highly conductive nanoscale electrical contacts suffer from strong current crowding and local hot spots due to nonuniform heat distribution, which severely affect the device properties. Here, we demonstrate a method to control the contact current distribution, by engineering the contact layer properties and geometry. From transmission line model calculations, we found that the contact current density greatly depends on the properties of the interfacial layer between two contacting members. The nonuniformity of the current distribution can be reduced significantly by strategically designing the interfacial layer specific contact resistivity p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>. The acute current crowding in ohmic contacts can be reduced greatly by parabolically varying the p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> along contact length, or by introducing a tunneling layer between the contact members. We also found that the current transport for 2D material based Schottky contacts can be improved by roughness engineering.

articleTitle: Lifetime of High-temperature Directly-heated Oxide Cathodes
abstract: In this paper we mainly describe the research progress in the lifetime testing for several kinds of high-temperature W base directly-heated oxide cathodes. The test results show that the lifetime of the 5% wt Sc<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> doped Y-Gd-Hf-O coating cathode is reached 6100h with a dc load of 1.0A/cm2 at 1500 °Cbr. The lifetime of the La2Hf207 coating cathode is beyond 11600h with a dc load of 0.65A/cm2 under 1400-1450°Cbr operating temperature. The lifetime of the Y2Zr207 coating cathode is also beyond 11600h with a dc load of 0.50 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> under same temperature.

articleTitle: Activation practice of GaAs(100) photocathodes with current-driven Cs/O dispensers
abstract: By adsorption of cesium and oxygen on GaAs(100) surface, negative electron affinity state can be realized to prepare superior photocathodes. Firstly, in view of the convenience of current-driven O dispensers, two types of current-driven O dispensers are investigated, and the sample activated by BaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based dispenser can obtain more effective <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${O}_{2}$</tex> release than that activated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Ag_{2}O$</tex> -based dispenser. Secondly, four groups of experiments are investigated, different Cs/O duration time are considered, the recipe of excessive O and non-excessive Cs is not suitable, while the recipe of continuous and completely excessive Cs along with intermittent and non-excessive O can achieve the best photoemission performance. Finally, to further understand if and how the illumination affects activation, another four groups of experiments under different monochromatic light are compared using the optimal activation recipe obtained, results show that sample activated under red light can obtain higher quantum efficiency and better stability.

articleTitle: Powerful terahertz pulsed large-orbit gyrotron for creating an intense ultraviolet plasma source
abstract: Implementation of an intense source of extreme ultraviolet radiation is possible on the basic of a gas-discharge plasma. The key point in this approach is a source of powerful terahertz pulses. We describe a modification of large-orbit pulsed gyrotron operating on the third cyclotron harmonic at the operating frequency of 1 THz. This modification allows increasing the output power of the gyrotron up to 4 kW.

articleTitle: A Broadband Suspended Coplanar Waveguide Slow wave Structure for Planar TWTs
abstract: In this paper, a wideband suspended coplanar waveguide (CPW) slow wave structure (SWS) for planar Traveling Wave Tubes (TWTs) is described with the analysis of its dispersion characteristics, interaction impedances and electric field distribution. Simulation results shows that the normalized phase velocity of the suspended CPW SWS changes only 0.007 for 26.5-40GHz, while the interaction impedances is higher than 12.7 Ohms. In addition, the existence of the metal ground plane can partly prevent the poorly-focused charges from hitting the dielectric substrate, which means the suspended CPW SWS is suitable for the design of broadband planar TWTs.

articleTitle: Calculation of Secondary Electron Yield of Alloys: Single Pole Approximation
abstract: Runaway secondary electrons can have detrimental effects on high power radio frequency devices used by the space industry. These runaway secondary electrons lead to a phenomenon known as the multipactor effect and the purpose of this work is to study the Secondary Electron Yield (SEY) of materials in an effort to find material properties which can help reduce the multipactor effect. In order to understand how alloying changes SEY, material properties of alloys CuNi, CuZn, and their component metals Cu, Ni, and Zn, are probed with the aid of Density Functional Theory (DFT). DFT is utilized in order to calculate the energy loss function (ELF), Fermi energy, density of states, and work function, all of which are used in a Monte Carlo simulation to calculate the SEY. In this work, the momentum dependency of the ELF is obtained using the Single Pole Approximation (SPA), an approximation often used to extrapolate the ELF calculated or measured for zero momentum transfer. Other work performed by our group, where the SEY of materials are simulated using momentum dependent ELFs calculated with the use of DFT, can be used to test the validity of the SPA.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon radiation source under the electron bunch excitation
abstract: Surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) are waves that propagate along the surface of a metal. The SPPs induced by electrons have the same phase velocity with the moving electrons. By altering the metal film width, the resonance of surface plasmon polaritons will slow the decay of SPPs with the time. The periodic change at the edge of the metal film will act as an antenna, radiating SPPs to the plane where the metal film is located. This detailed study ofthe resonant and radiation character of surface plasmons will be helpful to the optics circuit.

articleTitle: Free-Electron Masers Based on Excitation of Talbot-Type Supermodes
abstract: In powerful THz electron maser based on the use of a high-current relativistic electron beam, the use of an oversized cavity it inevitable. In this situation, it is difficult to provide selective excitation of a definite operating cavity mode. We propose to use excitation of a supermode formed by a fixed set of several transverse modes of an oversized waveguide due to the Talbot effect. We present designs of THz-frequency-range free-electron masers fed by a 10 MeV / 2 kA / 200 ns electron beam and based on excitation of a Talbot-type supermodes. The presentation includes results of our multi-frequency multi-mode simulations of the electron-wave interaction during the spatio-temporal process of formation and amplification of the supermode in oversized microwave systems. The calculated efficiency of these FEMs at the level of 5-10% corresponds to the GW level of the output power

articleTitle: Driving a Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillator with a Linear Transformer Driver
abstract: The Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillator (MILO) is a crossed-field device which uses a large (10s of kA) axial current to produce an azimuthal magnetic field. Coupled with a multi-cavity slow wave structure, this beam can produce microwave powers on the order of gigawatts. As a high-current, low-impedance device, the MILO may be profitably paired with a compact pulse power generator such as a Linear Transformer Driver (LTD). This paper presents results of simulations and experiments with this configuration.

articleTitle: Development and Modeling of a Multiple-Tunnel Meander-Line Slow-Wave Structure for a High-Power Millimeter-Band Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, we present the results of design, simulation, and fabrication of a multiple-tunnel slow-wave structure (SWS) for a high-power millimeter-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) with multiple sheet electron beams. Technology for microfabrication of the multiple-tunnel SWS is discussed. The results of fabrication and verification of the SWS are presented. Electromagnetic parameters of the SWS with different number of beam tunnels were simulated.

articleTitle: Design of a W-Band U-shaped Meander-line for Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: A W-band (88-98GHz) V-shaped meander-line for traveling wave tube (TWT) is analyzed in this paper. The U-shaped microstrip with conformal dielectric substrate is adopted to avoid charge hitting the dielectric substrate to a certain extent and accumulating. Furthermore, the microstrip slow wave structure (SWS) with conformal dielectric substrate has the higher interaction impedance than the SWS without it. The simulation results show that the proposed structure can provide an achievable gain up to 23.2dB and a maximum output power of 20.77W at 93GHz. The 3dB bandwidth is 7GHz from 89GHz to 96GHz.

articleTitle: 1-D Simulation of Backward-Wave and Pi-Mode Oscillations in Helix Traveling-Wave Tubes
abstract: A computationally efficient 1-D simulation tool for the prediction of backward-wave and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex>-mode oscillations in helix traveling-wave tubes is presented. The tool is based on modeling the circuit and the space-charge waves as coupled modes. The latter are obtained from an analytical model, the circuit-wave parameters from a separate simulation. An additional coupling between the circuit waves models delay-line asymmetries and enables the prediction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex>-mode oscillations. Oscillation frequencies and threshold currents agree well with those from a 3-D particle-in-cell simulation tool.

articleTitle: Development of a Ka-band 100-kW-Peak-Output-Power-Klystron with a 40% Beam-to-RF Conversion Efficiency
abstract: This paper presents the experiment results for a Ka-band klystron with a 100-kW peak output power level, which was developed in 2020. Three klystrons were built and tested. Over 100-kW-peak-output-power with a 50-MHz instantaneous bandwidth was measured at a 1% RF duty cycle (30-µs RF pulse-width and a 334-Hz repetition rate). The measured electron beam-to-RF conversion efficiency is 40%.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Dual-mode TWT
abstract: This paper describes the performance of a ka-band dual-mode TWT which operates at two modes (peak output power 300W at 10% duty and peak output power 100W at 70% duty).

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Compatibility in Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: Self-oscillation occurring in traveling wave tube (TWT) is discussed in this paper. The reason from perspective of electromagnetic compatibility is analyzed, and a general solution is proposed to improve reliability of traveling wave tube.

articleTitle: Space Power Combiner Based on Quasi-Optical Phase-Correcting Mirrors
abstract: This article proposes a space power combiner based on the quasi-optical phase-correcting technology. The combiner consists of a couple of irregular-shaped reflective mirrors, by which the wave generated from waveguide horns can be modulated into a Gaussian-like beam to achieve the space power combining. The deformation of the mirrors is calculated using a modified Katsenelenbaum–Semenov algorithm. Performance of the space power combiner evaluated by simulation, and the results indicate that the power combiner features high efficiency and broad bandwidth.

articleTitle: Optimization of a double-gap output cavity for a high efficiency klystron operating in the X-band
abstract: This paper presents the design of a double-gap output cavity for a klystron operating in the X band. First, the bunching circuit is presented. This bunching circuit provides a bunched electron beam used as the input for the final double-gap cavity design. Then two methods are presented to optimize this design, the first one is based on a clustering algorithm using a disk model simulation tool while the second one is based on a gradient descent using Particle In Cell (PIC) simulations. Both geometries provide about 65% efficiency.

articleTitle: Injection Locking of Different Axial Modes in the Second-Harmonic THz-Band Gyrotron
abstract: Injection locking of the 0.4-THz second-harmonic gyrotron by an external signal is studied by self-consistent numerical simulation. The locking of the fundamental mode (FM) as well as of the higher-order axial mode (HOAM) is investigated. The possibility of locking of different axial modes may be used for fast mode-switching operation.

articleTitle: Integrated photonic components for photoemission
abstract: Photoemission is one of the fundamental electron emission processes where a photon with high energy excites a thermal electron in the emitter material over the vacuum energy level and helps it escape into vacuum. There are three main limiting factors to achieving a high quantum efficiency (QE) in photoemission: (1) small optical absorption, (2) high energy photons and (2) energy loss in electrons while being transported to the emitting surface. In this work, we have shown that a thin GaAs film integrated on top of an integrated photonic component like ring resonator can absorb low energy photons with very high efficiency and achieve an ultrahigh absorbed optical power density of ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Such a high-power density can lead to electronic heating above the lattice temperature and provide high efficiency electron emission. This study can provide us a roadmap to designing integrated photonic components and experimentally achieving high QE photoemission.

articleTitle: Development of a 1-THz Fourth-Harmonic Gyrotron
abstract: Development of a fourth-harmonic gyrotron which uses a large-orbit gun and operates in 1000-GHz band is presented in this paper. The overall design of the gyrotron tube is introduced in detail. The large orbit gun is optimized with the concept of zero-velocity spread and achieves impressive parameters, including 80-kVvoltage, 0.7-A current, 1.5~1.8 pitch factor, ~5% velocity spread, and small guiding center spread. The facilities for the hot test of the gyrotron including the superconducting magnet system, power supply, spectrum meter, and power meter are almost ready. The proposed THz high-harmonic gyrotron is toward generation of 1-kW power around 1-THz band.

articleTitle: Including the Effects of Spatially Varying Work Functions in Electron Gun Design
abstract: We report on a new process under development in recent years that enables bringing the effects of detailed meso-scale thermionic emission properties to inform full-scale electron gun simulations. Specifically, detailed material properties and electrical properties of emitter samples are measured and processed, leading to a mapping of the work function across the emitter surface patch that is statistically applicable to the larger surface areas existing in a gun simulation. The measurements and processing subsequently leads to the development of Miram and IV curves for the material, as well as a prediction of the particle energy distribution and intrinsic emittance. Having this, we can then use these properties in simulations for high fidelity gun modeling for design applications. The process includes EBSD measurements, DFT simulations, then fast simulations using new 2-1/2D models from U. Wisconsin and U. Michigan 3D in collaboration with “first-principles” MICHELLE simulations, and will be presented.

articleTitle: Fabrication and test of a 5 GHz kladistron
abstract: A 5 GHz klystron of type “kladistron” has been designed and realized. It was adapted from the TH2166 from Thales, where the interaction line was transformed from 6 to 16 cavities. This klystron was fabricated and tested at Thales. The results of these tests are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Progress on a 71-76 GHz TWT
abstract: To address application requirements in satellite communications, a 71–76 GHz TWT has been designed based on a folded waveguide. Numerical simulations have predicted output power of up to 100 W with gain of 40 dB. An experiment is being prepared to test these predictions. The folded waveguide is micromachined in the copper alumium oxide composite material GLIDCOP and will be diffusion bonded and integrated with the electron gun, PPM focusing system, I/O windows and collector systems. The amplifier will operate with a single stage depressed collector to provide benchmarking of the simulations.

articleTitle: Latest Development of a Ka-band 500W Helix TWT for Satellite Communications
abstract: This paper introduced latest development of a Ka-Band 500W helix TWT for satellite communications systems, which is fulfilled at Beijing Vacuum Electronics Research Institute. Measurements show that the TWT is capable to deliver output power of more than 500W with a overall efficiency of 45% among the frequency of 27.5-31GHz. The maximum dimensions of the TWT were 330mm(L)×67mm(W) × 60mm(H) with a weight of 2.0kg(typical).

articleTitle: Theory, Simulation, and Experiments on Moderate-Current Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillators
abstract: The magnetically insulated line oscillator (MILO) is a high power microwave device, similar to the magnetron, that produces its own insulating magnetic field through large, driven current (typically> 30 kA) rather than from external magnets. At the University of Michigan, the Brillouin flow model of crossed field diodes has been greatly expanded to include the coaxial MILO geometry. It produces the Buneman-Hartree condition for the first time. The same theory, in tandem with particle-in-cell simulations via CST-Particle Studio, were applied to design a MILO for moderate-current operation (less than 10 kA) on MELBA-C, which is a −300 kV, 10 kA, microsecond Marx-Abramyan generator. Comparison between the theory, simulation, and experiments will be discussed in full, as well as output characteristics of the experiment.

articleTitle: A Fast Design and Optimization Method Based on Surrogate Model and Machine Learning
abstract: Design and optimize an electromagnetic device usually relies on the use of simulation software and intelligent optimization algorithm. Designer need to create a model of device, assign relevant design parameters, then the computer will instead of designer to simulate device and get the optimal result. But this method has some obvious disadvantages. First, how to create an appropriate model relies on designers' experience. Second, it costs a lot of time to do simulation calculations. Therefore, this method has long design cycles and low design efficiency. In order to overcome these weaknesses, this paper introduce a faster design method based on surrogate model and machine learning. Compared with the old method, it can be obviously found that the new method has lower computational complexity and higher convergence speed.

articleTitle: Initial Results of an S-Band Sheet Beam Klystron
abstract: A prototype S-band sheet beam klystron (SBK) has been successfully tested. Computer simulations were used in designing the SBK to help mitigate the well-known TE mode instability that has hampered previous efforts. During initial testing a 60 kV pulse to the electron gun resulted in a measured r.f. peak power of 6.1 MW. This is believed to be one of the first successful experimental demonstrations of such a device to operate without interference from the TE mode instability.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Electron Guns for a 220GHz Sheet Electron Beam EIK
abstract: We design two Pierce-type sheet beam electron guns with different compression ratios (the size of cathode narrow side divides the waist size of electron beam) with 4 and 10 respectively. Larger compression ratio means lower cathode current density which is easier to realize in the manufacture. However, larger compression ratio also means more powerful focusing ability which may cause edge distortion. For the comparison, above two different electron guns are designed thoroughly with the same parameters as following: beam voltage 16.5 kV, beam current 0.50 A, and beam waist size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1 \text{mm} \times 1.2\ \text{mm}$</tex>, which can be used in the development of 220 GHz extended interaction klystron (EIK). However, the cross section of compressed sheet beam shows obviously edge distortion phenomenon, which may affect the stable transmission of electron beam. Through the modeling and analysis with 3D software CST, it is found that we can shorten the size of the focusing electrode and adopt ellipse cathode to reduce edge distortion. Therefore, our study provides a method to optimize the Pierce-type sheet beam gun.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Particle Accelerator Components for a 10MeV Industrial Linac
abstract: This article presents the design of solenoid focusing magnet and steerer magnet to minimize beam loss in the drift space after the electron Linac exit. Scan horn is located at a distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 700mm from the Linac exit. Focusing magnet is designed such that beam is nearly parallel along the beam line. Transfer matrix method is employed to calculate required magnetic field that is 0.344 T. Same is verified by solving the beam envelope equation. Magnet size is optimized to get magnetic field of 0.34T using CST studio suite. Beam trajectory is evaluated using CST particle studio. X and Y steerer magnets are also designed using CST studio suite. At magnetic field of around 114 Gauss, beam deflection of 25 mm is observed. These findings form the framework of designing accelerators for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Pillared Meander Line Slow Wave Structure for W-band Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: The low beam voltage operation and the simple fabrication of meander lines make them a promising slow wave structure for the production of novel and low-cost traveling wave tubes for W-band satellite communications. However, the poor interaction of planar structures with a cylindrical beam has led to the investigation of alternative meander line configurations that could improve their performance. A novel slow wave structure based on adding pillars to a meander line for improving the interaction with a cylindrical electron beam is described. Simulations of the cold parameters and the large signal behavior are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Design and experiment of 140GHz high-order mode quasi-optical mode generator
abstract: In order to provide high-order input modes for low-power testing of gyrotron quasi-optical system, a mode generator for high-order modes TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28,8</inf> was designed based on the quasi-optical mode conversion theory. The simulation results show that the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28,8</inf> mode content of the designed quasi-optical mode generator reaches its highest 90.9% at the frequency of 140.18GHz. A measurement platform for the quasi-optical mode converter system is established and used in the local measurement of the mode generator. The cold test experiment showed that the resonant frequency of the generator was 140.155GHz, and the output mode field pattern is proved to be TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28,8</inf> mode.

articleTitle: Studies on G-band High-power Multi-beam Staggered Double Vane Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, a high efficiency and high-power staggered double vane slow wave structure travelling wave tube amplifier with double pencil beams is designed and studied carefully with good dispersion characteristics and interaction impedance. With a driven voltage of 20kV, a low driven current of 2*0.08A (603A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), a focusing H-field of 0.5T, this amplifier through 3D PIC simulation could get a 504W peak power and a 15.7% electron efficiency, gain of 40dB with a 30GHz bandwidth. This research could promote the development of millimeter and terahertz high-power vacuum electronic devices.

articleTitle: Design of a coaxial coupler for an E-band Helix Traveling-wave Tube
abstract: The performance of coupling system directly affects the bandwidth, power level and the efficiency of traveling-wave tube (TWT), so it is significant to match coupler structure and helix properly. In this paper, a coaxial coupler with matching cylinder for an E-band helix TWT is proposed. It is suitable for the case where there is a large characteristic impedance contrast between helix and the coaxial coupler. Based on the coupler structure, the voltage standing wave ratio(VSWR) of the E-band helix TWT decreases from 2.75 to 1.45 over the E-band range between 80 to 87 GHz.

articleTitle: High-Power Pulse Absorption using Metamaterial Absorber in Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, the processing of high-power pulse absorption using an ultra-broadband metamaterial absorber (UB-MMA) in Traveling wave tube (TWT) is investigated. This UB-MMA provides more than 90% absorptivity in the range of 8.00 GHz~19.40 GHz. The simulation results indicate that the significant local overheating phenomenon of the MMA is observed under 3000 W and 500 µs irradiation. It can be found that the local overheating is mainly concentrated at the corners and edges of the rectangular patterns on the surface of the MMA. And the temperature in these overheated areas can be as high as 380 K to 480 K. When exposed to 500 microseconds, the maximum temperature rises at a constant rate, which indicates the UB-MMA is an ather mal MMA. This study will be helpful for the usage of MMA as server in TWT.

articleTitle: Progress of 850GHz TWT Diamond Windows
abstract: This paper describes the design and fabrication of 850GHz TWT diamond windows by using single crystalline diamond and composite diamond films. For the metallization of the disks, the precision positioning and alignment technology were used to mask the central area. Both types of windows were assembled and tested. Comparison between their fabrication processes is given.

articleTitle: PICSEL: Particle-In-Cell Software for ELectromagnetism
abstract: In this paper, we present recent advances in simulation tools dedicated to linear beam tubes within THALES AVS. It details the work undertaken in the plateform PICSEL which contains softwares for gun, interaction structure and collector, and the first numerical results obtained. The main nolveties consist in the possibility of using hybrid mesh and high order resolutions for these softwares.

articleTitle: A Parameter Search Method For Optimal Efficiency Design Of High Power Millimeter Wave Gyrotron TWT
abstract: This paper introduces a method for searching the optimal efficiency parameters of high-power millimeter wave gyrotron based on BP neural network prediction. This method can establish the prediction model through the actual design gyrotron test data, and optimize the prediction model through the global optimization algorithm to obtain the optimal efficiency design parameters. This method can effectively extract accurate and effective information from the test data and feed back to the designers.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of 850GHz Defect Photonic Crystal Waveguide Slow Wave Structure
abstract: A defect photonic crystal waveguide (DPCW) slow wave structure (SWS) for wide band operation at 850GHz is proposed in this paper. The DPCW SWS is simplified to 3 transverse periods for the trade-off between processing difficulties and the ideal performance. Small signal simulation results show that 0.7W output power is obtained with 18.4kV beam voltage, 10mA beam current and 5mW input power. The prototypes for cold-test are fabricated using CNC precision milling and laser ablation technologies.

articleTitle: PIC Simulation of Multi-beam Terahertz Coaxial Resonator Reflex Klystron
abstract: In this paper, the particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation of a multi-beam terahertz (THz) coaxial resonator reflex klystron is conducted. When the currents of the beams are fixed as 5.7× 6 mA, the emission voltage of electron gun is set as 1.5 kV and the reflection voltage varies from 1.7kV to 2kV, the obtained output power varies from 0 to 700 mW and the signal frequency varies in the 130 MHz interval around 316.3 GHz, the maximum electron efficiency is about 1.36%. The output power of this reflex klystron is much higher than the traditional reflex klystron.

articleTitle: High-performance V-band Folded Waveguide TWT for satellite communication systems
abstract: In this paper, the design of a V-band high-performance folded-waveguide Traveling Wave Tube amplifier for next-generation high-data-rate satellite communication systems is presented. The folded waveguide shows a flat dispersion diagram and a high interaction impedance of about 5.95 Ω at the 49 GHz central frequency under a cathode voltage and beam current of 20.6 kVand 300 mA, respectively. Good performance in terms of output gain with a maximal value of 45 dB at the lower frequency of 47 GHz are obtained. COSMIC 1D large-signal analysis results are in good agreement with the simulated 3D PIC results. The TWT reaching a 5 GHz bandwidth with an almost constant maximum output power of about 600 W represents the best candidate for future uplink applications.

articleTitle: Progress of G-band CW transformed folded waveguide TWT
abstract: Institute of Applied Electronics has developed a wideband continuous waves (CW) transformed folded waveguide Traveling Wave Tube (TFWTWT) amplifier operating at G-band. The design and fabrication on CW TFWTWT was presented, including electronic-optical system, transformed folded waveguide slow wave structure (TFWSWS) and input/output (I/O) windows system. By the measurement, the amplifier produced the maximum output power 28.27W in frequency 220GHz with 7GHz −3dB bandwidth at CW work. The maximum gain is 31.4dB in frequency 221GHz.

Author Keywords: transformed folded waveguide slow wave structure

articleTitle: Possibilities of frequency tuning in gyrotrons with azimuthally-asymmetric cavities
abstract: An electrodynamic method based on azimuthally asymmetric cavities is proposed to provide a small frequency tuning in terahertz gyrotrons. The use of a cavity with a “close-to-circular” cross-section possessing small azimuthal inhomogeneities improves the selectivity of excitation of a high-cyclotron-harmonic wave. A small mechanical change of the transverse shape of this cavity changes the frequency of the operating wave with no affect on its transverse structure and rotation, and, therefore, on the electron-wave interaction.

articleTitle: Slow Wave Structure’ Internal Temperature Prediction Based on Experimental Data
abstract: At present, there are many researches on the thermal characteristics of traveling wave tubes (TWT), but few on the measurement of its internal temperature are involved because of the difficulty to monitor. The internal temperature, however, is closely related with the output power, reliability and stability of the tube. In this study, a simplified slow wave structure model was built and an RBF neural network was used to predict the internal temperature. The network was trained using the simulation temperature data from the corresponding ANSYS model. To verify the feasibility of the network, the external temperature of the simplified TWT model measured in the experiment were input into the model, and the error between the predicted and actual internal temperature was very small.

articleTitle: Research on a 3-D Microstrip Meander-line Slow-wave Structure Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: A three-dimensional microstrip meander-line slow-wave structure is proposed to reduce the risk of charge accumulation in a sheet beam traveling wave tube. And compared with the traditional planar meander-lline slow-wave structure, the interaction impedance of the 3-D microstrip meander-line SWS has been greatly improved. With the same structure parameters, taking 90GHZ as an example, the output power of the 3-D microstrip meander-line traveling wave tube (TWT) is about 10W higher than the traditional one, and the gain is about 2-dB higher.

articleTitle: 3D printed photopolymer structures with chemically deposited copper for microwave electronics
abstract: To create electrodynamic elements of microwave and millimeter-wave devices, the possibility of using the technology of photopolymer 3D printing with the subsequent surface metallization has been investigated. The applicability of the technology is considered by the example of prototypes of a profiled helical waveguide for a microwave undulator of a Compton free-electron laser and a periodic slow-wave structure of a backward-wave tube with a ribbon electron beam. The results of low-power measurements of the parameters of the indicated electrodynamic systems are in good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Powerful radiation source at 0.35 THz based on overmoded, periodic cavities
abstract: We present the design of a cylindrical, two-dimensional periodic surface lattice structure intended for use as the interaction region of an electron beam driven, pulsed Cherenkov source. We demonstrate production of high peak power radiation output at 0.35 THz. The interaction region is oversized and mode selection is achieved by the coupling of volume and surface fields to form a coupled cavity eigenmode. The work is also applicable to different frequencies, and the diameter of the cavity can be increased to achieve higher output powers.

articleTitle: Generation of Squeezed State Electron in Relativistic Magnetron by Using a Novel Cathode
abstract: An effective and practical method of forming low kinetic energy, high density state electrons in relativistic magnetron (RM) is proposed. By using a novel cathode structure, virtual cathode (VC) can be generated directly in a RM with almost all the output structure without magnetic mirror or radius variation, which lays a foundation for further experimental researches on RM driven by VC. Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation results show that when this novel cathode structure is used in an L-band all cavity axial extraction (ACAE) RM, an average output power of 700 MW with a power conversion efficiency of 61.4% can be achieved under a diode voltage of 600 kV.

articleTitle: The Effect of Angular Secondary Emission and Impact on Multipactor: Statistical Modeling and Threshold Analysis
abstract: Current theoretical approaches for efficient multipactor threshold analysis are mainly based on one-dimensional analytical model which only considers normal component of electron motion within multipactor process. This work presents an improved implementation method of multipactor statistical modeling by constructing the joint probability function with angular electron emission and impact regarded. On that basis, multipactor threshold calculation of both the parallel plates and coaxial lines are conducted and compared with the experimental results to quantitatively investigate the effect of angular secondary emission and impact on multipactor formation. Moreover, it also reveals that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$fd$</tex> (the product of the frequency and gap) scaling law stands for multipactor of coaxial lines with a constant radius ratio.

articleTitle: Study of the High-frequency System for a Ka-band EIK
abstract: A Ka-band continuous wave extended interaction klystron working in π mode is studied. The high-frequency characteristics of the resonant cavity and the beam-wave interaction of the extended interaction klystron are simulated and analyzed by using three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation software. The particle-in-cell simulation results show that the continuous wave output power of extended interaction klystron is 1350W at the frequency of 35GHz, the corresponding gain is 54dB, electronic efficiency is 27.6% at an operating voltage of 10kV and a beam current of 0.49A.

articleTitle: Efficient Compton FELs Based on Sectioned RF Undulator Systems
abstract: A high-efficiency regime of multi-stage trapping has been proposed for short-wavelength FELs recently. This scheme use strongly tapered RF undulator sections to be fed by phase-independent short-pulse high-power RF pulsed sources. In this work, we describe simulations of the realization of this multi-stage regime in short-wavelength SASE FELs, as well as profiled microwave systems designed for the realization of tapered rf undulators.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a metamaterial absorber for Folded Waveguide Slow Wave Structure
abstract: This paper demonstrates the experiment of a metamaterial absorber with lumped resistances, which can be used as sever for folded waveguide (FWG) slow wave structure (SWS). The experimental results fit well with the simulation results, and validate the theory we proposed in the previous work.

articleTitle: Physical Factors that Affect the Miram Curve
abstract: We present results from a semi-analytic model that solves the coupled Vlasov-Poisson equations in 3D assuming thermal electron emission with electron motions restricted to 1D by an infinite magnetic field. We examine how various 2D work function distributions on the cathode surface may impact the transition between temperature-limited and space-charge-limited emission, such as varying the fraction of non-emitting areas on the cathode surface, the emitting tile size, and the appearance of a few isolated, highly emitting “hot spots”.

articleTitle: Design of Coaxial-parallel Mode Converter Based on Iterative Method
abstract: As a high power source, the output mode of the gyrotron is usually TEon mode. As part of the high power output system, the mode converter plays a very important role. This article mainly introduces the method of converting TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode. The traditional TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode converter is calculated based on the coupled wave theory and designed by the axis function. This article is based on an iterative method. In order to obtain coaxial-parallel input and output ports, we can calculate by adding a structure optimization function.
